# Modular graph engine, Phase B3b: one protocol node per role, and the kernel deleted - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** the DSP kernel script node becomes one script node per role (the MIDI routing, mGB, the N8 FIFO, risa and
smsggdj host sync, LSDj sync and the controller session), placed by `buildGraph` with `kernelProjection` folded in;
`rp.host.midi-out` takes each input's system from its settings instead of a 4-byte prefix; zod leaves the script-node
bundle behind a zod-free settings schema that `defineNode` takes; and `DspKernel`, the kernel node and the roles'
behaviours are deleted. Bit-identical to the parity baseline at every task, with nothing re-recorded.

**Architecture:** Per [docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md](modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md). A zod-free `s`
schema (`graph/settingsSchema.ts`) parses and writes its JSON Schema as its zod twin does, and `defineNode` takes it
beside zod's. Seven script node types (`src/script/nodes/`) are each a role's glue ported line for line around the
protocol's unchanged pure functions, written against the `Block` API with nothing allocated per warm block, every
type reshaping, every capacity the kernel node's, port for port. `rp.host.midi-out` gains a `systems` form, an input
per producer, each input's messages under its entry's system. The kernel node's C++ rig runs every case on the
kernel's graph and on the per-role one, which holds every recorded digest. Then `buildGraph` places the routing, the
controller and a protocol node per role ahead of the systems, from a model holding the MIDI routing, the controller
(its app config parsed by the publisher) and each system's protocol roles, which a registry-free table
(`graph/protocolNodes.ts`) maps from role kinds. The kernel and everything only it used go, zod with them, and the
script host labels each script node's span by its type.

**Tech stack:** TypeScript on txiki (`pnpm test` mock tier, `pnpm test:native` real host), the script host's bare
QuickJS (esbuild and the in-tree `tjsc` for bytecode), C++20 with Catch2 (`retroplug-engine-graph-test`), the graph
layer of Phases A to B3a.

**Provenance:** every code block below was built and run before this plan was written, on the scratch branch
`proto/b3b` in this worktree, on top of the design commit 5e6b9962: eight commits, one per task (Task 9 is the
acceptance run and commits nothing), with GCC 13.3 on linux-x64 (a Ryzen 9 9950X). A code block that creates a file
is that file as the prototype commit left it; one that changes files is the prototype's diff for them, so `git apply`
it from the step's text (or apply it hunk by hunk with the Edit tool). One file a command writes is not shown: the
`buildGraph` goldens Task 5 re-records. The two one-off scripts that re-record and check them were never committed;
they are quoted from the prototype's scratch directory. Task 8's comment changes to 31 `test-native` files are checked
out of the prototype commit rather than quoted (the step says why). Every expected pass, test count and benchmark

**Where this plan departs from the design.** The design as committed (5e6b9962) was written before the prototype,
and building it changed some of what it says; the plan follows what was built, and Task 8's docs commit lands the
amended design with a new section 9, "Found while building". Host MIDI out's `systems` form (Task 3) comes before the
equivalence rig (Task 4), where section 7 had them the other way: the rig builds the per-role document, and without
the systems form that document cannot say whose host MIDI is whose, since no protocol node writes the 4-byte prefix.
Its inputs are `in1` to `inN`, 1-based as `rp.core.merge`'s, at most 128, under any 32-bit id, one id possibly
repeated; until Task 6 an empty list is the old prefixed form, after it a node with no inputs. The role-to-node
mapping section 4 left open is a table, `graph/protocolNodes.ts`, pure, zod-free and registry-free, not a `node` field
on `RoleType`: the node types are a fact of the bundle every Engine embeds, and two of the three publishers that need
the mapping hold no registry (a `DirectGraph`, and a `SystemsStore` built without one). The controller's app config is
parsed by the publisher (`ProjectStore.controllerModel`, `DirectGraph.setController`, both through
`controller/registry.ts`'s `parseAppConfig`), where section 3 had `buildGraph` parse it, so `buildGraph` stays pure
and registry-free; the target resolution and the MI.MAP override live in `graph/controller.ts`, and `kernelProjection`
goes in the flip (Task 5) rather than the deletion. The N8 node's input is `midiIn`, not `midi` (its output is named
for the system input it feeds, and a port id names one port), and the routing node's outputs are `sys-<id>`, its
layout refusing one id twice. The settings schema's method is `safeParse` (zod's), an array's item carries a default of
its own, and `s.json` takes its type as an explicit parameter. The `midi-routing` and `launchpad` roles go in Task 6
with `RoleType`'s `dsp` and `scope` and `isSystemStage`, since only the kernel read them as roles, and
`DirectGraph.setProjectStages`, kept through the flip, gives way to `setMidiRouting` and `setController`. The planner
already keeps document order among nodes ready at once, so the profile build's `apu-render` span needs no fix
(section 4 left it to check). Two things the design did not foresee: a temporary TS cross-check drives `DspKernel`
and the nodes through the same blocks (Task 2, deleted with the kernel in Task 6), and the rig gains one case recorded
from the kernel node (Task 4), since three of section 5's orders were ones no recorded case sent a message through.
Task 7 names each script node's span by its type and drops the JS span globals only the kernel's roles used (the
`[profile]` cases go from five to four), drops the bench's unconsumed mGB serial-out stand-in and adds an MI.OUT row,
and has the profile benches prove their counters live by the peak heap, which the allocation-free nodes made
necessary. Task 8 renames spec/04 to `04-roles-protocol-nodes.md`.

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**
- Commit after each task (the commit commands are given; Task 9 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed,
  in a commit of its own). No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" trailer.
- Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context and removed lines of older code): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the
  session itself.
- Don't `rm -rf build` to fix CMake; investigate. Never use bare `git stash`, and never switch branches with
  uncommitted work in the tree. A new or removed CMake source needs a reconfigure first: `cmake -S . -B build`
  (Task 6 renames one).
- `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure. That is the tracked audio patch: expected, leave it.
- The derived bundle C arrays (`build/native/*bundle_data.c`) are never committed.
- No parity baseline is recorded anywhere in B3b, and no digest in the kernel node's rig (`KernelNode.test.cpp`, then
  `ProtocolNodes.test.cpp`) is changed: every task leaves every baseline and every recorded value passing unchanged.
  A parity failure is a real change to the audio, and a digest that fails is a real change to what reaches a core or
  the host: stop and find it. The skip baseline does not move either.
- The fixture groups need `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources`; without it their cases skip. Pass it on
  the same command line: a shell `export` does not survive between commands.
- `node packages/retroplug/scripts/run-native-tests.mjs` (what `pnpm test:native` runs) takes ONE filter: an exact
  slug (`parity/lsdj-sync`) or a prefix in the dash form (`parity-blocks-tiny`; `parity/blocks-tiny` matches
  nothing). Run several files as separate commands, or the whole suite.
- The CI view is `test:native` UNFILTERED with the fixture directories absent:
  `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/nonexistent-rp-resources RISA_SRC=/nonexistent-rp-risa pnpm test:native`. Only an
  unfiltered run judges the skip baseline, so a filtered one proves nothing about it.
- The profile build's `dsp-bench` (`tools/run-profile.sh stats`, in `build-prof/`) fails from Task 6 until Task 7:
  its check that its counters are live needs an allocation, and once the kernel is gone the nodes make none in a warm
  block. Nothing in the default suites runs it, and Task 7 changes the check; do not run it in between.
- `git checkout <prototype commit> -- <paths>` is used once, in Task 8, for the paths that step lists and no others;
  the branch `proto/b3b` must stay until this plan has been executed.
- While a Reaper check runs it uses `build/bin`: do not rebuild the plugin until it finishes. Run the Reaper checks
  one at a time, and before each make sure no Reaper or jackd of an earlier run is left (`pgrep -a reaper;
  pgrep -a jackd`).
- `pnpm check:docs` counts the tracked docs: 58 in the prototype, which had no plan file, so 59 once this plan is
  committed.

### Task 1: A zod-free settings schema, and the toy nodes on it

Zod is most of the script-node bundle (about 567 KB of its 660 KB) though the audio side never checks a setting, and
MicroQuickJS cannot carry it at all (design section 3). `src/graph/settingsSchema.ts` is the part of zod a node's
settings use, and no more: `s.object`, `s.enum(values, default)`, `s.int({ min, max, default })`, `s.bool(default)`,
`s.number(default)`, `s.string(default)`, `s.array(item, default)` and `s.json<T>(default)`, behind the `safeParse` /
`toJSONSchema` pair `defineNode` reads. Each does what its zod twin does with the same shape: zod's result and issue
shape, the first issue's message word for word, unknown keys stripped as `z.object` strips them, and the JSON Schema
zod's `toJSONSchema({ io: "input" })` writes, key for key (an `s.int` writes its bounds, the safe-integer range where
none is given, as zod's `.int()` does). An array's item takes a default of its own, never used to parse but written
into the schema as zod writes an item's `.default`; `s.json` takes its type as an explicit parameter, since a default
such as `{}` says nothing about it. It keeps to ES5's library, so it is no obstacle to MicroQuickJS.

`defineNode` takes any `SettingsSchema`, so a zod schema still serves (the kernel node keeps its own until Task 6),
and imports no zod at all; `define-node.test.ts` keeps one zod case on purpose. The script test bundle's echo node and
the native tests' fifteen JS toy nodes move onto `s` (`rp.s` for `rp.z`), `rp.toy.transformed`, whose settings
transform, getting a hand-written `{ safeParse, toJSONSchema }`; the test bundle then carries no zod (588942 bytes to
21537). The production bundle is byte-identical.

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/settings-schema.test.ts`
- Modify: `packages/native/test/engine-graph/ScriptNodes.test.cpp`, `packages/retroplug/src/graph/defineNode.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/define-node.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/script/scriptTestBundle.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

`settings-schema.test.ts` holds every builder, and nesting, to zod's own output: the JSON Schema of each shape, and
what each parses or refuses across 34 values, the refusal's words included. `define-node.test.ts` moves onto `s`,
keeping one zod case; the native tests' toy nodes take `rp.s`, which the test bundle now hands them:

Create `packages/retroplug/test/graph/settings-schema.test.ts`:

````ts
// The zod-free settings schema (src/graph/settingsSchema.ts), held to zod: each builder against its zod twin (the same
// shape, each field with a .default), for the JSON Schema it writes and for what defineNode makes of a document's
// settings through it, defaults filled and refusals worded alike.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { z } from "zod";
import { defineNode, events } from "../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { s, type Infer, type Schema, type SettingsParseResult, type SettingsSchema } from "../../src/graph/settingsSchema";

const noop = () => ({ process() {} });
const show = (v: unknown): string => (typeof v === "number" ? String(v) : (JSON.stringify(v) ?? String(v)));

// A refusal's first issue, where and why.
function first(result: SettingsParseResult<unknown>): { path: readonly PropertyKey[]; message: string } {
  if (result.success) throw new Error(`expected a refusal, got ${show(result.data)}`);
  const issue = result.error.issues[0];
  return { path: issue.path, message: issue.message };
}

// Each builder, and its zod twin. Every one is a field of a root object below, as a node's settings field is.
const twins: { name: string; mine: Schema<unknown>; zod: z.ZodType }[] = [
  { name: "int", mine: s.int({ min: 1, max: 4, default: 2 }), zod: z.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(2) },
  { name: "int with a min", mine: s.int({ min: 0, default: 0 }), zod: z.number().int().min(0).default(0) },
  { name: "int with a max", mine: s.int({ max: 0xffffffff, default: 1 }), zod: z.number().int().max(0xffffffff).default(1) },
  { name: "int with no bounds", mine: s.int({ default: 3 }), zod: z.number().int().default(3) },
  { name: "int past the safe range", mine: s.int({ min: -1e20, max: 1e20, default: 0 }), zod: z.number().int().min(-1e20).max(1e20).default(0) },
  { name: "number", mine: s.number(0.5), zod: z.number().default(0.5) },
  { name: "string", mine: s.string("x"), zod: z.string().default("x") },
  { name: "bool", mine: s.bool(true), zod: z.boolean().default(true) },
  {
    name: "enum",
    mine: s.enum(["off", "midiSync", "masterSync"], "midiSync"),
    zod: z.enum(["off", "midiSync", "masterSync"]).default("midiSync"),
  },
  { name: "enum of one", mine: s.enum(["only"], "only"), zod: z.enum(["only"]).default("only") },
  {
    name: "array",
    mine: s.array(s.int({ min: 0, max: 9, default: 0 }), [1, 2]),
    zod: z.array(z.number().int().min(0).max(9).default(0)).default([1, 2]),
  },
  {
    name: "array of objects",
    mine: s.array(s.object({ id: s.int({ min: 1, default: 1 }), on: s.bool(false) }), []),
    zod: z.array(z.object({ id: z.number().int().min(1).default(1), on: z.boolean().default(false) }).default({ id: 1, on: false })).default([]),
  },
  { name: "json", mine: s.json({ a: [1, { b: 2 }] }), zod: z.unknown().default({ a: [1, { b: 2 }] }) },
  { name: "json null", mine: s.json(null), zod: z.unknown().default(null) },
  {
    name: "object in an object",
    mine: s.object({ x: s.number(1), deep: s.object({ y: s.string(""), ids: s.array(s.int({ default: 0 }), [7]) }) }),
    zod: z
      .object({
        x: z.number().default(1),
        deep: z.object({ y: z.string().default(""), ids: z.array(z.number().int().default(0)).default([7]) }).default({ y: "", ids: [7] }),
      })
      .default({ x: 1, deep: { y: "", ids: [7] } }),
  },
];

const input = { io: "input" } as const;

test("each builder, as a field, writes the JSON Schema its zod twin writes, key for key", () => {
  for (const t of twins)
    expect(s.object({ f: t.mine }).toJSONSchema(input), t.name).toEqual(z.object({ f: t.zod }).toJSONSchema(input));
});

test("an object of every builder writes them in its shape's order, as zod does", () => {
  const mine: Record<string, Schema<unknown>> = {};
  const zod: Record<string, z.ZodType> = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < twins.length; ++i) {
    mine[`f${twins.length - i}`] = twins[i].mine;  // keys not in sorted order, so the order is the shape's
    zod[`f${twins.length - i}`] = twins[i].zod;
  }
  const written = s.object(mine).toJSONSchema(input);
  expect(written).toEqual(z.object(zod).toJSONSchema(input));
  // The input schema: no field is required, and no additionalProperties, so a key it does not name is allowed.
  expect(Object.keys(written)).toEqual(["$schema", "type", "properties"]);
});

test("the root takes no default, so its JSON Schema writes none, as zod's twin with none at its root", () => {
  expect(s.object({}).toJSONSchema(input)).toEqual(z.object({}).toJSONSchema(input));
  expect(s.int({ min: 1, max: 4, default: 2 }).toJSONSchema(input)).toEqual(z.number().int().min(1).max(4).toJSONSchema(input));
  expect(s.enum(["a", "b"], "a").toJSONSchema(input)).toEqual(z.enum(["a", "b"]).toJSONSchema(input));
  const root = { mine: s.object({ n: s.int({ min: 1, default: 1 }) }), zod: z.object({ n: z.number().int().min(1).default(1) }) };
  expect(first(root.mine.safeParse(undefined))).toEqual(first(root.zod.safeParse(undefined)));
  expect(first(root.mine.safeParse(undefined))).toEqual({ path: [], message: "Invalid input: expected object, received undefined" });
});

// What defineNode makes of a document's settings through a schema: the settings, or the one line it throws.
function outcome(settings: SettingsSchema<unknown>, raw: unknown): string {
  const node = defineNode({ id: "rp.test.settings", settings, ports: {}, create: noop });
  try {
    return `ok ${JSON.stringify(node.parseSettings(raw))}`;
  } catch (e) {
    return `refused ${(e as Error).message}`;
  }
}

// Every value tried on every builder: the right type for some, the wrong one for the rest.
const values: unknown[] = [
  undefined, null, true, false, 0, 2, -1, 9, 2.5, 2 ** 53, -(2 ** 53), 1e300, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, "", "x", "2",
  "midiSync", "only", [], [1, 2], [1, 10, "x"], [{}], [{ id: 2 }], [{ id: "x" }], [null], {}, { y: 5 }, { x: 2 },
  { x: 2, deep: { y: "z", ids: [1, 2.5] } }, { x: "y" }, { deep: [] }, { a: [1] },
];

test("defineNode makes the same of every value through each builder as through its zod twin", () => {
  for (const t of twins) {
    const mine = s.object({ f: t.mine });
    const zod = z.object({ f: t.zod });
    expect(outcome(mine, {}), `${t.name}: nothing`).toBe(outcome(zod, {}));
    for (const v of values) expect(outcome(mine, { f: v }), `${t.name}: ${show(v)}`).toBe(outcome(zod, { f: v }));
  }
});

test("a refusal's first issue has zod's path and message, in the shape's order", () => {
  const mine = s.object({ a: s.int({ min: 1, max: 4, default: 2 }), list: s.array(s.object({ id: s.int({ default: 1 }) }), []) });
  const zod = z.object({
    a: z.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(2),
    list: z.array(z.object({ id: z.number().int().default(1) })).default([]),
  });
  for (const raw of [{ list: [{ id: 1 }, { id: 0.5 }], a: 9 }, { list: [{}, { id: "1" }] }, { list: [{ id: 1 }, null] }, 5, [], null, "x"])
    expect(first(mine.safeParse(raw)), show(raw)).toEqual(first(zod.safeParse(raw)));
  expect(first(mine.safeParse({ list: [{}, { id: "1" }] }))).toEqual({ path: ["list", 1, "id"], message: "Invalid input: expected number, received string" });
  expect(outcome(mine, { list: [{}, { id: 2.5 }] })).toBe(`refused node type "rp.test.settings": settings: list.1.id: Invalid input: expected int, received number`);
  // Every field is checked, in shape order, whatever order the document writes them in.
  const two = mine.safeParse({ list: {}, a: "x" });
  expect(two.success ? [] : two.error.issues.map((i) => i.path.join("."))).toEqual(["a", "list"]);
});

test("the words for each refusal, as zod words them", () => {
  const n = s.object({
    i: s.int({ min: 1, max: 4, default: 2 }),
    e: s.enum(["a", "b"], "a"),
    one: s.enum(["only"], "only"),
    b: s.bool(false),
    list: s.array(s.string(""), []),
  });
  const why = (raw: Record<string, unknown>) => outcome(n, raw).replace(`refused node type "rp.test.settings": settings: `, "");
  expect(why({ i: 9 })).toBe("i: Too big: expected number to be <=4");
  expect(why({ i: 0 })).toBe("i: Too small: expected number to be >=1");
  expect(why({ i: 1.5 })).toBe("i: Invalid input: expected int, received number");
  expect(why({ i: 2 ** 53 })).toBe("i: Too big: expected int to be <=9007199254740991");
  expect(why({ i: "2" })).toBe("i: Invalid input: expected number, received string");
  expect(why({ i: NaN })).toBe("i: Invalid input: expected number, received NaN");
  expect(why({ e: "c" })).toBe(`e: Invalid option: expected one of "a"|"b"`);
  expect(why({ one: "two" })).toBe(`one: Invalid input: expected "only"`);
  expect(why({ b: "true" })).toBe("b: Invalid input: expected boolean, received string");
  expect(why({ list: [1] })).toBe("list.0: Invalid input: expected string, received number");
  expect(why({ list: null })).toBe("list: Invalid input: expected array, received null");
});

test("an object drops a key its shape does not name, at every depth, as z.object strips it", () => {
  const mine = s.object({ a: s.int({ default: 1 }), o: s.object({ b: s.bool(false) }), list: s.array(s.object({ c: s.string("") }), []) });
  const zod = z.object({
    a: z.number().int().default(1),
    o: z.object({ b: z.boolean().default(false) }).default({ b: false }),
    list: z.array(z.object({ c: z.string().default("") })).default([]),
  });
  const raw = { extra: 1, a: 2, o: { b: true, more: [1] }, list: [{ c: "x", d: 4 }, { e: null }] };
  const parsed = mine.safeParse(raw);
  expect(parsed).toEqual({ success: true, data: { a: 2, o: { b: true }, list: [{ c: "x" }, { c: "" }] } });
  expect(parsed.success && parsed.data).toEqual(zod.parse(raw));
});

test("parse fills each default, keeps each value given, and hands back objects of the caller's own", () => {
  const n = s.object({
    i: s.int({ default: 3 }),
    list: s.array(s.int({ default: 0 }), [1, 2]),
    deep: s.object({ tags: s.array(s.string(""), ["t"]) }),
    config: s.json<{ rows: number[] }>({ rows: [4] }),
  });
  const defaults = { success: true, data: { i: 3, list: [1, 2], deep: { tags: ["t"] }, config: { rows: [4] } } };
  const filled = n.safeParse({});
  expect(filled).toEqual(defaults);
  if (!filled.success) return;
  filled.data.list.push(9);
  filled.data.deep.tags.push("u");
  filled.data.config.rows.push(5);
  expect(n.safeParse({})).toEqual(defaults);
  // A value given is kept, and a json value as given, as z.unknown keeps it.
  const config = { rows: [1], other: "kept" };
  const given = n.safeParse({ i: -5, list: [], deep: { tags: [] }, config });
  expect(given).toEqual({ success: true, data: { i: -5, list: [], deep: { tags: [] }, config: { rows: [1], other: "kept" } } });
  expect(given.success && given.data.config).toBe(config);
});

test("a default its own schema refuses is refused when the schema is made", () => {
  expect(() => s.int({ min: 1, max: 4, default: 9 })).toThrow("a settings default must pass its own schema: Too big: expected number to be <=4");
  expect(() => s.int({ default: 0.5 })).toThrow("expected int");
  expect(() => s.enum(["a", "b"], "c" as never)).toThrow(`expected one of "a"|"b"`);
  expect(() => s.array(s.int({ min: 0, default: 0 }), [1, -1])).toThrow("Too small: expected number to be >=0");
  expect(() => s.number(Infinity)).toThrow("expected number");
});

// The settings type, as z.infer gives it: a compile-time check (a mismatch fails pnpm typecheck).
type Equal<A, B> = (<T>() => T extends A ? 1 : 2) extends <T>() => T extends B ? 1 : 2 ? true : false;
const settings = s.object({
  mode: s.enum(["off", "midiSync"], "off"),
  divisor: s.int({ min: 1, max: 16, default: 1 }),
  start: s.bool(false),
  gain: s.number(0),
  name: s.string(""),
  ids: s.array(s.int({ default: 1 }), []),
  inner: s.object({ on: s.bool(true) }),
  config: s.json<{ app: string }>({ app: "x" }),
});
const inferred: Equal<
  Infer<typeof settings>,
  { mode: "off" | "midiSync"; divisor: number; start: boolean; gain: number; name: string; ids: number[]; inner: { on: boolean }; config: { app: string } }
> = true;

test("the settings type is inferred, and a node's create and ports receive it", () => {
  expect(inferred).toBe(true);
  const node = defineNode({
    id: "rp.test.typed",
    settings,
    ports: (o) => ({ out: events.out({ messages: o.divisor }) }),
    create: ({ settings: o }) => ({ process: () => void o.inner.on }),
  });
  const typed: Equal<ReturnType<typeof node.parseSettings>, Infer<typeof settings>> = true;
  expect(typed).toBe(true);
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema.ts`:

````ts
// Node settings without zod (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md section 3). A bundle of script nodes is loaded
// into both of an Engine's QuickJS runtimes, the control side that checks settings and lays out ports and the audio
// side that runs process, and zod was most of it (about 567 KB of 660 KB) though the audio side never checks a thing;
// MicroQuickJS (the Pico) cannot carry it at all. This is the part of zod a node's settings use, and no more:
//
//   const settings = s.object({
//     mode: s.enum(["off", "midiSync", "masterSync"], "off"),
//     tempoDivisor: s.int({ min: 1, max: 16, default: 1 }),
//     autoStart: s.bool(false),
//   });
//   type Settings = Infer<typeof settings>;  // { mode: "off" | "midiSync" | "masterSync"; tempoDivisor: number; ... }
//
// defineNode takes any SettingsSchema, so a zod schema serves as well; zod stays where the app uses it on the control
// plane (the role configs, the project files). Each builder does what its zod twin does with the same shape (z.object,
// z.enum, z.number().int().min().max(), z.boolean(), z.number(), z.string(), z.array(), z.unknown(), each field with a
// .default), held to zod's own output by test/graph/settings-schema.test.ts:
//
// - safeParse returns zod's result, each issue with zod's path and zod's English message, word for word, so
//   defineNode's one-line `field: why` reads the same. Every field is checked, in shape order, and a value refused
//   gets one issue: the first zod reports for it.
// - Every schema has a default, which a field (or an array item) takes when it is missing or undefined; an object's is
//   its fields' defaults. The value safeParse is handed is never missing (parseSettings reads nothing as {}), so the
//   root takes no default and its JSON Schema writes none, as zod's twin has none at its root. An item's default is
//   never used to parse, but is written to the JSON Schema, as zod writes an item's .default.
// - An object drops a key its shape does not name, as z.object does: it strips, and refuses nothing. So a document may
//   carry a field this build does not read (one a later version adds) and still be read, and its input JSON Schema
//   says as much by writing no additionalProperties. A C++ node's settings (rfl::DefaultIfMissing) ignore one too.
// - A value is checked, never coerced: "2" is no int. An int is a safe integer, as zod's .int() requires.
// - toJSONSchema writes what zod's toJSONSchema({ io: "input" }) writes, key for key and in its order: the schema of
//   what a document may write, so no field is required. It is the only form there is.
// - A default is copied each time it is taken, and an object or array parsed is a new one, so what safeParse returns
//   is the caller's to edit. A json value given is kept as given, as z.unknown keeps it.
//
// It keeps to ES5's library (no Object.entries, includes, Number.isInteger and the like), as src/controller/portable.ts
// does, so it is no obstacle to MicroQuickJS; defineNode itself is not there yet.

/** A refusal, as a zod issue carries one: where (the field names and item indices from the root), and why. */
export interface SettingsIssue {
  readonly path: readonly PropertyKey[];
  readonly message: string;
}

export type SettingsParseResult<T> =
  | { success: true; data: T }
  | { success: false; error: { issues: readonly SettingsIssue[] } };

/** What defineNode takes as a node's settings: an `s` schema, or a zod one, which has the same two methods.
 *  safeParse fills defaults and refuses with issues; toJSONSchema({ io: "input" }) is the descriptor's settings. */
export interface SettingsSchema<T> {
  safeParse(raw: unknown): SettingsParseResult<T>;
  toJSONSchema(opts: { io: "input" }): unknown;
}

type Path = (string | number)[];
type Issues = { path: Path; message: string }[];
/** Checks a value that is present: the value to keep, or an issue pushed (and what it returns is not used). */
type Check<T> = (value: unknown, path: Path, issues: Issues) => T;
type Keywords = Record<string, unknown>;

const MAX_SAFE = 9007199254740991;  // Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, which ES5 has no name for
const DIALECT = "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema";

const hasOwn = (o: object, key: string): boolean => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o, key);

// A fresh copy of a JSON value, so a default taken is the caller's own.
function copy<T>(value: T): T {
  if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") return value;
  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    const out: unknown[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < value.length; ++i) out.push(copy(value[i]));
    return out as T;
  }
  const from = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  const keys = Object.keys(from);
  for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) out[keys[i]] = copy(from[keys[i]]);
  return out as T;
}

// zod's name for what it was given, in an invalid_type issue: the typeof, but for "NaN", "null" and "array". (zod also
// names a class instance by its constructor, which no JSON holds.)
function received(value: unknown): string {
  if (value === null) return "null";
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return "array";
  if (typeof value === "number" && value !== value) return "NaN";
  return typeof value;
}

const invalidType = (expected: string, value: unknown): string => `Invalid input: expected ${expected}, received ${received(value)}`;

/** One schema, made by the builders on `s`. */
export class Schema<T> implements SettingsSchema<T> {
  private readonly fallback: T;
  private readonly check: Check<T>;
  /** Its own JSON Schema keywords, in zod's order: all but the default, which the object or array holding it writes. */
  private readonly keywords: () => Keywords;

  /** A default its own check refuses is a mistake in the definition, refused here rather than at every parse. The
   *  default is copied, so the caller's own value is never the one taken. */
  constructor(fallback: T, check: Check<T>, keywords: () => Keywords) {
    this.fallback = copy(fallback);
    this.check = check;
    this.keywords = keywords;
    const issues: Issues = [];
    check(fallback, [], issues);
    if (issues.length > 0) throw new Error(`a settings default must pass its own schema: ${issues[0].message}`);
  }

  safeParse(raw: unknown): SettingsParseResult<T> {
    const issues: Issues = [];
    const data = this.check(raw, [], issues);
    return issues.length > 0 ? { success: false, error: { issues } } : { success: true, data };
  }

  /** What zod's toJSONSchema({ io: "input" }) writes, whatever is asked: the input form is the only one. */
  toJSONSchema(_opts?: { io?: "input" }): Keywords {
    return { $schema: DIALECT, ...this.keywords() };
  }

  /** A field's or an item's value: its default when it is missing, else the value checked. */
  read(value: unknown, path: Path, issues: Issues): T {
    return value === undefined ? copy(this.fallback) : this.check(value, path, issues);
  }

  /** A field's or an item's JSON Schema: its default first, where zod writes a .default, then its own keywords. */
  describe(): Keywords {
    return { default: copy(this.fallback), ...this.keywords() };
  }
}

/** The settings type a schema gives, as z.infer gives a zod schema's. */
export type Infer<S> = S extends Schema<infer T> ? T : never;

type Fields = Record<string, Schema<unknown>>;

function object<F extends Fields>(fields: F): Schema<{ [K in keyof F]: Infer<F[K]> }> {
  type Out = { [K in keyof F]: Infer<F[K]> };
  const keys = Object.keys(fields);
  const check: Check<Out> = (value, path, issues) => {
    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    if (value === null || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) {
      issues.push({ path, message: invalidType("object", value) });
      return out as Out;
    }
    const given = value as Record<string, unknown>;
    // Own keys only, where zod reads inherited ones too: a field named for an Object.prototype member (toString)
    // given no value is missing, not that member. JSON has no inherited keys, so a document reads the same either way.
    for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) {
      const key = keys[i];
      out[key] = fields[key].read(hasOwn(given, key) ? given[key] : undefined, path.concat(key), issues);
    }
    return out as Out;
  };
  // Its default is what it reads from an empty object: each field's.
  return new Schema(check({}, [], []), check, () => {
    const properties: Keywords = {};
    for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) properties[keys[i]] = fields[keys[i]].describe();
    return { type: "object", properties };
  });
}

// A value of one JSON type, refused as zod refuses any other.
function primitive<T>(type: string, is: (value: unknown) => boolean, fallback: T): Schema<T> {
  const check: Check<T> = (value, path, issues) => {
    if (!is(value)) issues.push({ path, message: invalidType(type, value) });
    return value as T;
  };
  return new Schema(fallback, check, () => ({ type }));
}

// z.number() refuses NaN and both infinities (an infinity as "received number", zod's words).
const isNumber = (value: unknown): value is number => typeof value === "number" && isFinite(value);

/** A whole number, a safe integer, from min to max when they are given. */
function int(o: { min?: number; max?: number; default: number }): Schema<number> {
  const { min, max } = o;
  // In zod's order: the type, then .int() (whole, then safe), then .min(), then .max().
  const check: Check<number> = (value, path, issues) => {
    const why = !isNumber(value) ? invalidType("number", value)
      : Math.floor(value) !== value ? invalidType("int", value)
      : value > MAX_SAFE ? `Too big: expected int to be <=${MAX_SAFE}`
      : value < -MAX_SAFE ? `Too small: expected int to be >=${-MAX_SAFE}`
      : min !== undefined && value < min ? `Too small: expected number to be >=${min}`
      : max !== undefined && value > max ? `Too big: expected number to be <=${max}`
      : null;
    if (why !== null) issues.push({ path, message: why });
    return value as number;
  };
  // zod writes both bounds for an int, the safe range's where none is given or the safe range is tighter.
  return new Schema(o.default, check, () => ({
    type: "integer",
    minimum: min !== undefined && min > -MAX_SAFE ? min : -MAX_SAFE,
    maximum: max !== undefined && max < MAX_SAFE ? max : MAX_SAFE,
  }));
}

/** One of a list of strings. */
function oneOf<const V extends readonly [string, ...string[]]>(values: V, fallback: NoInfer<V[number]>): Schema<V[number]> {
  const list: string[] = values.slice();
  // zod's words: one value alone is expected outright, more are listed quoted and joined by "|".
  const why = list.length === 1
    ? `Invalid input: expected "${list[0]}"`
    : `Invalid option: expected one of ${list.map((v) => `"${v}"`).join("|")}`;
  const check: Check<V[number]> = (value, path, issues) => {
    if (typeof value !== "string" || list.indexOf(value) < 0) issues.push({ path, message: why });
    return value as V[number];
  };
  return new Schema(fallback, check, () => ({ type: "string", enum: list.slice() }));
}

/** A list of items of one schema. */
function array<T>(item: Schema<T>, fallback: readonly T[]): Schema<T[]> {
  const check: Check<T[]> = (value, path, issues) => {
    const out: T[] = [];
    if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
      issues.push({ path, message: invalidType("array", value) });
      return out;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < value.length; ++i) out.push(item.read(value[i], path.concat(i), issues));
    return out;
  };
  return new Schema(fallback as T[], check, () => ({ type: "array", items: item.describe() }));
}

/** An opaque JSON value, already checked where it was made (a controller's parsed app config, say): any value is
 *  kept, and its JSON Schema says nothing but its default. Its type is the caller's to name: s.json<AppConfig>(...). */
function json<T = unknown>(fallback: T): Schema<T> {
  return new Schema(fallback, (value) => value as T, () => ({}));
}

/** The builders. Each takes its default; s.object's is its fields'. */
export const s = {
  object,
  enum: oneOf,
  int,
  bool: (fallback: boolean): Schema<boolean> => primitive("boolean", (v) => typeof v === "boolean", fallback),
  number: (fallback: number): Schema<number> => primitive("number", isNumber, fallback),
  string: (fallback: string): Schema<string> => primitive("string", (v) => typeof v === "string", fallback),
  array,
  json,
};
````

### Task 2: One script node per role, beside the kernel

The seven node types of design section 2, in `src/script/nodes/`, registered in the script bundle after
`rp.dsp.kernel`, which still runs every block: no document places them yet, and parity does not move. Each is its
role's glue ported line for line around the protocol's pure parts, which stay where they were (the routing
arithmetic, now also an allocation-free `routeTarget` over a message's bytes; the Arduinoboy and master-sync
decoders; `risaLocate`; the SMS levels; `walkTicks`), written against the `Block` API as `rp.bench.pass` is: indexed
loops over the input views, `send` on the node's own ports, its state and tick counter on the instance. Every type
reshapes, so a config edit keeps the instance and its state, and each port's capacity is the kernel node's
(`nodes/ports.ts`, which `kernelNode.ts` now reads: `serialIn` and `midi` 4096 messages / 72 KiB, `bytes` 256 / 1 KiB,
`buttons` 64 / 128 bytes, `midiOut` 1024 / 8 KiB, `controllerOut` 256 / 4 KiB), with a routing output at
`rp.host.midi-in`'s 2048 / 64 KiB and `launches` at 64 messages / 256 bytes.

- `rp.midi.route`: settings `mode` and `systems` (the ids in slot order); an output per system, `sys-<id>`, in slot
  order; a layout naming one id twice is refused, as the kernel's zod settings refused it with a refinement.
- `rp.mgb.midi`: each MIDI message's bytes as one `serialIn` message at its frame, where the kernel coalesced all
  same-frame bytes (a system node applies a message's bytes in order, and the digests hash `serialIn` byte by byte).
- `rp.n8.midi-to-fifo`: input `midiIn`, output `midi`, named for the system input it feeds.
- `rp.risa.sync` and `rp.sms.sync` (`machine`): bytes from the transport alone, risa's arm a flushing message as the
  kernel sent it.
- `rp.lsdj.sync` (`mode`, `tempoDivisor`, `autoStart`): reads its routed `midi` and then its `launches` as one inbox,
  in that order, as the kernel's inbox held them; groups its fed-back `serialOut` as runs of same-frame bytes, as the
  kernel did; sends `serialIn`, `buttons` (a 2-byte `[button, down]` at frame 0) and `midiOut` (every message at
  frame 0). Master sync's state stays in the sub-object the mode dispatcher drops outside the mode.
- `rp.controller.session`: settings `app`, `target`, the resolved `systemId` (0 none), the parsed `appConfig`, the
  `songRowTicks` table and the anchor; it parses nothing. Its launches go out at frame 0, on `launches` for a
  "system" target and on `midiOut` for "midiOut". The controller apps' runtime moves to a zod-free
  `controller/apps/index.ts` (`CONTROLLER_APPS`, `controllerApp(id)`), which the node imports; the registry pairs each
  runtime with its menu label and zod schema, and refuses, when it registers, an app with none.

Two more zod-free splits keep the kernel's modules out of the nodes: `walkTicks` moves to `src/ticks.ts`
(`dspKernel.ts` re-exports it until Task 6), and the LSDj link bytes and `midiMapRow` to `src/lsdjSyncBytes.ts`, out
of `dspRoles.ts` and its schemas. The seven alone are about 77 KB of bundle, none of it zod.

The node-level tests port the role tests that drive `DspKernel` (roles, LSDj modes, routing, risa, sms, the
controller, ticks, the kernel-level MI.OUT and master-sync cases), one file per type, over a `Block` stand-in
(`test/script/nodes/_rig.ts`). A temporary `kernel-equivalence.test.ts`, deleted with the kernel, drives `DspKernel`
and the per-role nodes through the same blocks (1-frame, ragged and 1024-frame blocks, transport starts, stops and
seeks, tempo changes, MIDI at block edges, MI.OUT and master-sync bytes, a controller session, routing in every mode,
config edits mid-run) and compares every port; it caught 29 of 30 deliberate mutations of the nodes. Where the nodes
cannot match the kernel and no parity case can see it (a role's state keyed by its kind, the controller's default
target following a change of first system, a session rebuilt on its parsed config, launches only into
`rp.lsdj.sync`, `onSettings` only on a real change, store-parsed configs needed, a throw stopping only its node), the

````ts
// A script node driven as the script host drives one (packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.cpp), over a stand-in
// for its Block: settings parsed on the control side and crossed as JSON, a plan swap's onSettings only when they
// changed, and a block that holds the node to its layout. What the stand-in models:
//
// - messages, send and control take only a port the layout has, of the method's kind, and throw a TypeError for
//   another, as the host does; every Block method throws once the process call it was handed to has returned.
// - send copies the data (each value & 0xff) and records the frame twice: as sent, and as the port's queue holds it,
//   raised to the last frame sent on that port this block.
// - The messages a block hands out are the node's for that call only: their bytes are scribbled over once it returns,
//   so a node that kept a view past the block reads garbage, as it would from the host's refilled buffers.
import type { Block, ControlStream, DefinedNode, Message, NodeInstance } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import type { Layout } from "../../../src/graph/descriptor";

/** An input message as a test writes it. */
export interface In {
  frame: number;
  data: number[];
  flags?: number;
}

/** One send, in the order the node made it. */
export interface Sent {
  port: string;
  /** The frame the node sent. */
  frame: number;
  /** The frame the port's queue holds it at: raised to the last one sent on the port this block. */
  queued: number;
  data: number[];
  flags: number;
}

export interface BlockSpec {
  frames: number;
  playing?: boolean;
  ppq?: number;
  tempo?: number;
  sampleRate?: number;
  inputs?: Record<string, readonly In[]>;
  controls?: Record<string, ControlStream>;
}

const json = <T>(v: T): T => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v)) as T;

export class NodeRig<S> {
  node: NodeInstance<S>;
  settings: S;
  private layout: Layout;
  /** How many instances create made: 1, and one more for each settings change the definition does not reshape. */
  creates = 1;
  /** The last block's sends, kept when its process threw. */
  last: Sent[] = [];

  constructor(
    readonly def: DefinedNode<S>,
    raw: unknown = {},
    readonly sampleRate = 44100,
    readonly maxFrames = 8192,
  ) {
    this.settings = json(def.parseSettings(raw));
    this.layout = def.layout(this.settings);
    this.node = def.create({ settings: this.settings, sampleRate, maxFrames });
  }

  /** New settings at a plan swap. Unchanged ones (by their JSON) are no change, and reach no hook; a changed layout
   *  without `reshapes` is a new instance. True when the node saw the change. */
  set(raw: unknown): boolean {
    const next = json(this.def.parseSettings(raw));
    if (JSON.stringify(next) === JSON.stringify(this.settings)) return false;
    const layout = this.def.layout(next);
    const reshaped = JSON.stringify(layout) !== JSON.stringify(this.layout);
    this.settings = next;
    this.layout = layout;
    if (reshaped && this.def.reshapes !== true) {
      this.node = this.def.create({ settings: json(next), sampleRate: this.sampleRate, maxFrames: this.maxFrames });
      this.creates++;
    } else {
      this.node.onSettings?.(json(next));
    }
    return true;
  }

  /** The layout's port ids, as `dir kind id`. */
  ports(): string[] {
    return this.layout.ports.map((p) => `${p.dir} ${p.kind} ${p.id}`);
  }

  /** One block, and every send it made. A throw from process is the caller's, the sends before it kept in `last`. */
  run(spec: BlockSpec): Sent[] {
    const sent: Sent[] = [];
    this.last = sent;
    const ports = this.layout.ports;
    const port = (id: unknown, dir: "in" | "out", kinds: readonly string[], what: string) => {
      const p = ports.find((q) => q.id === id && q.dir === dir && kinds.includes(q.kind));
      if (!p) throw new TypeError(`${this.def.id} has no ${what} ${String(id)}`);
      return p;
    };
    let live = true;
    const alive = () => {
      if (!live) throw new TypeError("a block is used only during its node's process call");
    };
    const handedOut: Uint8Array[] = [];
    const lastFrame = new Map<string, number>();
    const block: Block = {
      frames: spec.frames,
      transport: { sampleRate: spec.sampleRate ?? 44100, tempo: spec.tempo ?? 120, ppq: spec.ppq ?? 0, playing: spec.playing ?? false },
      audio: () => {
        throw new TypeError("no audio ports here");
      },
      messages: (id) => {
        alive();
        port(id, "in", ["events", "bytes"], "events or bytes input");
        return (spec.inputs?.[id] ?? []).map((m): Message => {
          const data = Uint8Array.from(m.data);
          handedOut.push(data);
          return { frame: m.frame, data, flags: m.flags ?? 0 };
        });
      },
      send: (id, frame, data, flags = 0) => {
        alive();
        port(id, "out", ["events", "bytes"], "events or bytes output");
        const at = frame >>> 0;
        const queued = Math.max(at, lastFrame.get(id) ?? 0);
        lastFrame.set(id, queued);
        sent.push({ port: id, frame: at, queued, data: Array.from(data, (v) => v & 0xff), flags: flags >>> 0 });
        return true;
      },
      control: (id) => {
        alive();
        port(id, "in", ["control"], "control input or param");
        return spec.controls?.[id] ?? { start: 0, changes: [] };
      },
      emit: () => {
        throw new TypeError("no control outputs here");
      },
    };
    try {
      this.node.process(block);
    } finally {
      live = false;
      for (const d of handedOut) d.fill(0xee);
    }
    return sent;
  }
}

/** The sends on `port`, each as [queued frame, ...bytes]. */
export const on = (sent: readonly Sent[], port: string): number[][] => sent.filter((s) => s.port === port).map((s) => [s.queued, ...s.data]);

/** The bytes sent on `port`, each as [queued frame, byte]: how a serial-in port is compared, byte by byte. */
export const bytesOn = (sent: readonly Sent[], port: string): [number, number][] => {
  const out: [number, number][] = [];
  for (const s of sent) if (s.port === port) for (const b of s.data) out.push([s.queued, b]);
  return out;
};
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/script/nodes/midi-route.test.ts`:

````ts
// rp.midi.route (src/script/nodes/midiRoute.ts): the host's MIDI fanned to one output a system, by the routing mode.
// The expectations of test/dsp/routing.test.ts, which drives the midi-routing role through the kernel, at the node,
// and each mode's decision held to routeBlock, the pure oracle.
import { test, expect } from "../../../testing/harness";
import { MIDI_ROUTE_NODE_TYPE, midiRouteNode } from "../../../src/script/nodes/midiRoute";
import { routeBlock, MIDI_ROUTING_VALUES, type MidiEvent } from "../../../src/midiRouting";
import { NodeRig, on, type In } from "./_rig";

const route = (mode: string, systems: number[]) => new NodeRig(midiRouteNode, { mode, systems });

test("one output a system, named by its id, in slot order, after the one input", () => {
  expect(new NodeRig(midiRouteNode).ports()).toEqual(["in events midiIn"]);
  expect(route("sendToAll", [7, 3, 0xffffffff]).ports()).toEqual([
    "in events midiIn",
    "out events sys-7",
    "out events sys-3",
    "out events sys-4294967295",
  ]);
  const d = midiRouteNode.descriptor();
  expect(d.id).toBe(MIDI_ROUTE_NODE_TYPE);
  // Each output holds what rp.host.midi-in's does, since under send-to-all it carries all of it.
  expect(midiRouteNode.layout(midiRouteNode.parseSettings({ systems: [1] })).ports[1].capacity).toEqual({ messages: 2048, bytes: 65536 });
  expect(midiRouteNode.reshapes).toBe(true);
});

test("settings default to send-to-all and no systems, and refuse a bad mode, a bad id or one id twice", () => {
  expect(midiRouteNode.parseSettings({})).toEqual({ mode: "sendToAll", systems: [] });
  expect(() => midiRouteNode.parseSettings({ mode: "everywhere" })).toThrow("mode: Invalid option");
  for (const id of [0, 1.5, -1, 2 ** 32]) expect(() => midiRouteNode.parseSettings({ systems: [id] }), `id ${id}`).toThrow("systems.0");
  expect(() => midiRouteNode.layout(midiRouteNode.parseSettings({ systems: [4, 4] }))).toThrow("rp.midi.route: two systems have the id 4");
});

test("OneChannelPerInstance sends each channel to its system, at its frame", () => {
  const sent = route("oneChannelPerInstance", [10, 20]).run({
    frames: 1024,
    inputs: {
      midiIn: [
        { frame: 0, data: [0x90, 60, 100] }, // channel 0 → system index 0 (id 10)
        { frame: 3, data: [0x91, 62, 80] }, //  channel 1 → system index 1 (id 20)
      ],
    },
  });
  expect(on(sent, "sys-10")).toEqual([[0, 0x90, 60, 100]]);
  expect(on(sent, "sys-20")).toEqual([[3, 0x91, 62, 80]]);
});

test("with no systems, nothing is sent", () => {
  expect(route("sendToAll", []).run({ frames: 1024, inputs: { midiIn: [{ frame: 0, data: [0x90, 60, 100] }] } })).toEqual([]);
});

test("SysEx and system messages reach every system unchanged, in every mode; an empty message reaches none", () => {
  const sysex = [0xf0, 0x7d, 1, 2, 3, 0xf7];
  for (const mode of MIDI_ROUTING_VALUES) {
    const sent = route(mode, [1, 2]).run({
      frames: 64,
      inputs: { midiIn: [{ frame: 1, data: sysex }, { frame: 2, data: [0xf8] }, { frame: 3, data: [] }, { frame: 4, data: [0x93, 1, 2, 3, 4] }] },
    });
    // Five bytes is SysEx's length, whatever its status says (native rides it on dataExt), so it is broadcast too.
    for (const port of ["sys-1", "sys-2"]) expect(on(sent, port), `${mode} ${port}`).toEqual([[1, ...sysex], [2, 0xf8], [4, 0x93, 1, 2, 3, 4]]);
  }
});

test("MidiChannelToInstance's target takes the message with its channel rewritten to 0, and no other system does", () => {
  const sent = route("midiChannelToInstance", [1, 2, 3]).run({
    frames: 64,
    inputs: { midiIn: [{ frame: 0, data: [0x94, 60, 100] }, { frame: 1, data: [0xc2, 7] }, { frame: 2, data: [0xb5, 1] }] },
  });
  expect(on(sent, "sys-1")).toEqual([]);
  expect(on(sent, "sys-2")).toEqual([[0, 0x90, 60, 100]]); // channel 4 % 3 = 1
  expect(on(sent, "sys-3")).toEqual([[1, 0xc0, 7], [2, 0xb0, 1]]); // channels 2 and 5
});

test("every mode routes as routeBlock does, over 1 to 3 systems and every channel", () => {
  const events: In[] = [];
  for (let ch = 0; ch < 16; ch++) events.push({ frame: ch * 3, data: [0x90 | ch, 40 + ch, 100] }, { frame: ch * 3 + 1, data: [0xe0 | ch, 0, 64] });
  events.push({ frame: 60, data: [0xfa] }, { frame: 61, data: [0xf0, 1, 2, 3, 0xf7] });
  for (const mode of MIDI_ROUTING_VALUES) {
    for (let n = 1; n <= 3; n++) {
      const ids = [5, 9, 2].slice(0, n);
      const sent = route(mode, ids).run({ frames: 128, inputs: { midiIn: events } });
      const expected = routeBlock(events as MidiEvent[], mode, n);
      ids.forEach((id, i) => expect(on(sent, `sys-${id}`), `${mode} ${n} systems, #${i}`).toEqual(expected[i].map((e) => [e.frame, ...e.data])));
    }
  }
});

test("a settings change moves the routing on the next block: a new mode, and the outputs reordered", () => {
  const rig = route("oneChannelPerInstance", [1, 2]);
  const block = { frames: 64, inputs: { midiIn: [{ frame: 0, data: [0x91, 60, 100] }] } };
  expect(on(rig.run(block), "sys-2")).toEqual([[0, 0x91, 60, 100]]);
  expect(rig.set({ mode: "oneChannelPerInstance", systems: [2, 1] })).toBe(true); // channel 1 is now system 1's
  expect(on(rig.run(block), "sys-1")).toEqual([[0, 0x91, 60, 100]]);
  rig.set({ mode: "midiChannelToInstance", systems: [2, 1] });
  expect(on(rig.run(block), "sys-1")).toEqual([[0, 0x90, 60, 100]]);
  expect(rig.creates).toBe(1); // reshaped, never made again
});
````

// rp.mgb.midi (src/script/nodes/mgbMidi.ts): every routed MIDI byte into the Game Boy's serial input. The mgb case of
// test/dsp/roles.test.ts, which drives the role through the kernel, at the node.
import { test, expect } from "../../../testing/harness";
import { MGB_MIDI_NODE_TYPE, mgbMidiNode } from "../../../src/script/nodes/mgbMidi";
import { NodeRig, bytesOn, on } from "./_rig";

test("its routed MIDI in, the serial input out, sized as the kernel's serial-in port", () => {
  const rig = new NodeRig(mgbMidiNode);
  expect(rig.ports()).toEqual(["in events midi", "out bytes serialIn"]);
  expect(mgbMidiNode.descriptor().id).toBe(MGB_MIDI_NODE_TYPE);
  expect(mgbMidiNode.layout({} as never).ports[1].capacity).toEqual({ messages: 4096, bytes: 73728 });
  expect(mgbMidiNode.reshapes).toBe(true);
});

test("mgb forwards each routed MIDI byte to its system's serial, at its message's frame", () => {
  const sent = new NodeRig(mgbMidiNode).run({ frames: 22050, inputs: { midi: [{ frame: 0, data: [0x90, 60, 100] }] } });
  expect(bytesOn(sent, "serialIn")).toEqual([[0, 0x90], [0, 60], [0, 100]]);
});

test("a message goes as one serial-in message, at its frame, and an empty one as none", () => {
  const sent = new NodeRig(mgbMidiNode).run({
    frames: 1024,
    inputs: { midi: [{ frame: 9, data: [0x90, 60, 100] }, { frame: 9, data: [0xb0, 1, 64] }, { frame: 10, data: [] }, { frame: 200, data: [0xf0, 1, 2, 3, 0xf7] }] },
  });
  expect(on(sent, "serialIn")).toEqual([[9, 0x90, 60, 100], [9, 0xb0, 1, 64], [200, 0xf0, 1, 2, 3, 0xf7]]);
  expect(sent.every((s) => s.flags === 0)).toBe(true);
});

test("nothing in, nothing out, whatever the transport", () => {
  const rig = new NodeRig(mgbMidiNode);
  expect(rig.run({ frames: 1024, playing: true })).toEqual([]);
  expect(rig.run({ frames: 1024, playing: false })).toEqual([]);
});
