Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/ports.ts`:

````ts
// What the protocol script nodes' outputs hold in one block, at most, and the bytes-message flag one of them sends
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md section 5). The capacities are the DSP kernel node's, port for port
// (script/kernelNode.ts takes its own from here until it goes), since each protocol node's output carries what that
// kernel output carried for its system; a queue drops what does not fit, and the drop is counted per port.
import type { QueueCapacity } from "../../graph/descriptor";

/** RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH (graph/rp_node.h): a bytes message the device takes only after dropping what it still holds. */
export const FLUSH = 1;

// The two that pass host MIDI on, serial in (mGB, lsdj-sync's passthrough) and core MIDI (nes-n8-midi), each hold at
// least what rp.host.midi-in's output holds (kHostMidiInMessages and kHostMidiInBytes, host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp), so
// the one place host MIDI is dropped is that edge. Core MIDI takes a message for each forwarded one; serial in at most
// one for each forwarded message, plus the sync roles' own bytes. Both have room for 4096 messages and 72 KiB: twice
// rp.host.midi-in's messages, and its bytes with 8 KiB more for a role's own (a sync role's clock and row bytes, in a
// block whose forwarded MIDI fills rp.host.midi-in), so a SysEx the host stages whole (a sample upload to a NES build)
// reaches the system whole. (The most the suites sent through them in one block, measured over test:native with the
// fixtures, parity included, 2.2 million kernel blocks up to 8192 frames: per system, 18 serial-in bytes and 8
// core-MIDI messages holding 4096 bytes, the largest 512.)
//
// The rest are sized from the same measurement: per system, 11 core-byte messages holding 11 bytes, 1 button press;
// 14 host MIDI-out messages holding 70 bytes with the kernel's 4-byte system prefixes; 5 control-surface messages
// holding 206 bytes (in one). dsp-bench's densest profile, skipped there, sends 13 messages of 39 bytes a block. Each
// of these has room for 16 times the messages or more, and the bytes as well, but for the MIDI out's (a decoded MI.OUT
// stream at its densest, a captured byte every 8 frames: 1024 in 8192). A queue costs 16 bytes a message plus its
// bytes, per plan.
export const SERIAL_IN: QueueCapacity = { messages: 4096, bytes: 73728 };
export const CORE_MIDI: QueueCapacity = { messages: 4096, bytes: 73728 };
export const CORE_BYTES: QueueCapacity = { messages: 256, bytes: 1024 };
export const BUTTONS: QueueCapacity = { messages: 64, bytes: 128 };
export const MIDI_OUT: QueueCapacity = { messages: 1024, bytes: 8192 };
export const CONTROLLER_OUT: QueueCapacity = { messages: 256, bytes: 4096 };

/** A routing output: under send-to-all it carries everything rp.host.midi-in's output passed, so it holds as much
 *  (kHostMidiInMessages and kHostMidiInBytes). */
export const ROUTED_MIDI: QueueCapacity = { messages: 2048, bytes: 65536 };

/** The controller's launches into its target's lsdj-sync node: a 3-byte row launch or release for each pad a player
 *  pressed this block, which is a handful at most. */
export const LAUNCHES: QueueCapacity = { messages: 64, bytes: 256 };
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/clock.ts`:

````ts
// A protocol node's tick clock: the drift-free counter the DSP kernel kept for each system (its `tick` map), kept on
// the node's instance instead. No system has two clocking protocols, so one counter a node is the counter its system
// had. Made once in create, filled each block, so a block allocates nothing here.
import type { Block } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import { walkTicks, type TickBlock, type TickCallback } from "../../ticks";

export class TickClock {
  /** This block's transport, as a tick walk reads it (and as master sync reads the block's length and rate). */
  readonly block: TickBlock = { frames: 0, sampleRate: 44100, tempo: 120, ppqStart: 0, transport: false };
  /** The tick the next walk starts from: 0 on a fresh instance, as the kernel's counter was for a new system. */
  next = 0;

  /** Read this block's transport. Called once at the top of every process, before any walk. */
  begin(b: Block): void {
    const t = b.transport;
    const into = this.block;
    into.frames = b.frames;
    into.sampleRate = t.sampleRate;
    into.tempo = t.tempo;
    into.ppqStart = t.ppq;
    into.transport = t.playing;
  }

  /** Each tick this block holds at `resolution` ticks a quarter, through `cb`, and the counter advanced past them: the
   *  kernel's ctx.eachTick. A walk `cb` throws out of leaves the counter where it was, as the kernel's did. */
  walk(resolution: number, cb: TickCallback): void {
    this.next = walkTicks(this.block, resolution, this.next, cb);
  }
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/midiRoute.ts`:

````ts
// The host's MIDI fanned out to the systems (the `midi-routing` role's DSP behaviour, dspRoles.ts, as a script node):
// one output a system, named by its id, in slot order, since the modes but send-to-all route by a channel's position
// among them. Each message goes to its systems at its own frame, in the order it came, by routeTarget's arithmetic
// (midiRouting.ts), the decision the kernel's routeBlockInto makes; MidiChannelToInstance's target takes a copy with
// the channel rewritten to 0.
//
// Allocation-free: a message goes on as the view the block handed over, and a rewritten one from a 4-byte buffer
// made once, through a view of each length made with it. Only a settings change makes the port ids again.
import { defineNode, events, type PortSpec } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import { s, type Infer } from "../../graph/settingsSchema";
import { MIDI_DATA_SIZE, MIDI_ROUTING_VALUES, MidiRouting, ROUTE_ALL, routeTarget } from "../../midiRouting";
import { ROUTED_MIDI } from "./ports";

export const MIDI_ROUTE_NODE_TYPE = "rp.midi.route";

const settings = s.object({
  mode: s.enum(MIDI_ROUTING_VALUES, "sendToAll"),
  /** The systems' ids, in slot order: each has an output, `sys-<id>`, in this order. */
  systems: s.array(s.int({ min: 1, max: 0xffffffff, default: 1 }), []),
});

export type MidiRouteSettings = Infer<typeof settings>;

/** The output a system's MIDI leaves by. */
export const routedPort = (system: number): string => `sys-${system}`;

const outputsOf = (systems: readonly number[]): string[] => systems.map(routedPort);

export const midiRouteNode = defineNode<MidiRouteSettings>({
  id: MIDI_ROUTE_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "MIDI Routing",
  category: "midi",
  settings,
  reshapes: true,
  // Two systems with one id would be one output fed twice, so the layout refuses them (the settings schema has no
  // way to say so, where the kernel's zod settings refined it).
  ports: (s) => {
    const p: Record<string, PortSpec> = { midiIn: events.in() };
    for (const id of s.systems) {
      const port = routedPort(id);
      if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(p, port)) throw new Error(`${MIDI_ROUTE_NODE_TYPE}: two systems have the id ${id}`);
      p[port] = events.out(ROUTED_MIDI);
    }
    return p;
  },
  create: ({ settings: initial }) => {
    let mode = initial.mode;
    let outputs = outputsOf(initial.systems);
    const rewritten = new Uint8Array(MIDI_DATA_SIZE);
    const byLength: Uint8Array[] = [];
    for (let n = 0; n <= MIDI_DATA_SIZE; n++) byLength.push(rewritten.subarray(0, n));
    return {
      process(b) {
        const count = outputs.length;
        if (count === 0) return;
        const messages = b.messages("midiIn");
        for (let e = 0; e < messages.length; e++) {
          const m = messages[e];
          const data = m.data;
          const target = routeTarget(data, mode, count);
          if (target === ROUTE_ALL) {
            for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) b.send(outputs[i], m.frame, data);
          } else if (target >= 0) {
            if (mode === MidiRouting.MidiChannelToInstance) {
              // Only a channel message reaches here in this mode (SysEx and system messages go to every system),
              // so it is at most MIDI_DATA_SIZE bytes.
              rewritten[0] = data[0] & 0xf0;
              for (let j = 1; j < data.length; j++) rewritten[j] = data[j];
              b.send(outputs[target], m.frame, byLength[data.length]);
            } else {
              b.send(outputs[target], m.frame, data);
            }
          }
        }
      },
      onSettings(next) {
        mode = next.mode;
        outputs = outputsOf(next.systems);
      },
    };
  },
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/mgbMidi.ts`:

````ts
// mGB's MIDI (the `mgb` role's DSP behaviour, dspRoles.ts, as a script node): every routed MIDI byte goes into the
// Game Boy's serial input at its message's frame, which is all mGB listens for. A message goes as one serial-in
// message of its bytes, where the kernel sent a run of same-frame bytes as one: the system node applies a message's
// bytes in order at its frame, so the bytes the core sees, and when, are the same. Sends the view the block handed
// over, so a block allocates nothing.
import { bytes, defineNode, events } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import { SERIAL_IN } from "./ports";

export const MGB_MIDI_NODE_TYPE = "rp.mgb.midi";

export const mgbMidiNode = defineNode({
  id: MGB_MIDI_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "mGB MIDI",
  category: "protocol",
  reshapes: true,
  ports: { midi: events.in(), serialIn: bytes.out(SERIAL_IN) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const messages = b.messages("midi");
      for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) {
        const m = messages[i];
        if (m.data.length > 0) b.send("serialIn", m.frame, m.data);
      }
    },
  }),
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/n8MidiToFifo.ts`:

````ts
// A NES's MIDI (the `nes-n8-midi` role's DSP behaviour, dspRoles.ts, as a script node): every routed MIDI message goes
// on whole to the core's MIDI input, which feeds the always-attached N8 FIFO (the NES core's NesN8FifoRole iterates
// the bytes into it). The NES twin of rp.mgb.midi: a core with no serial port receives MIDI here instead. Sends the
// view the block handed over, so a block allocates nothing.
//
// Its output is named for the system node's input it is wired to, `midi`, as every protocol node's is; a port id
// names one port, so its input, the routed MIDI the other protocol nodes call `midi`, is `midiIn` here.
import { defineNode, events } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import { CORE_MIDI } from "./ports";

export const N8_MIDI_TO_FIFO_NODE_TYPE = "rp.n8.midi-to-fifo";

export const n8MidiToFifoNode = defineNode({
  id: N8_MIDI_TO_FIFO_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "N8 MIDI to FIFO",
  category: "protocol",
  reshapes: true,
  ports: { midiIn: events.in(), midi: events.out(CORE_MIDI) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const messages = b.messages("midiIn");
      for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) b.send("midi", messages[i].frame, messages[i].data);
    },
  }),
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/risaSync.ts`:

````ts
// risa's host sync (the `risa-sync` role's DSP behaviour, dspRoles.ts, as a script node): the DAW transport into
// risa's N8-FIFO receive path, a raw byte protocol that reuses MIDI status values (risaSync.ts). On a transport rise,
// or a ppqStart discontinuity while playing (a seek or a loop), a fresh 5-byte arm+locate computed from ppqStart, which
// flushes the FIFO, then START; on a fall, STOP; while playing, 24-PPQN clocks at their own frames (the FIFO has no
// serial gate). The arm points the clock at the clock after the one it names, which risa primes itself.
//
// The role's glue, line for line, with its state and its system's tick counter on the instance. A block allocates
// nothing but an arm's packet, as the role's did.
import { bytes, defineNode, type Block } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import {
  RISA_CLOCK,
  RISA_PPQN,
  RISA_SEEK_TOLERANCE,
  RISA_START,
  RISA_STOP,
  risaArmPacket,
  risaLocate,
} from "../../risaSync";
import { TickClock } from "./clock";
import { CORE_BYTES, FLUSH } from "./ports";

export const RISA_SYNC_NODE_TYPE = "rp.risa.sync";

const START = new Uint8Array([RISA_START]);
const STOP = new Uint8Array([RISA_STOP]);
const CLOCK = new Uint8Array([RISA_CLOCK]);

export const risaSyncNode = defineNode({
  id: RISA_SYNC_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "risa Host Sync",
  category: "protocol",
  reshapes: true,
  ports: { bytes: bytes.out(CORE_BYTES) },
  create: () => {
    const clock = new TickClock();
    let prevT = false;
    let ppqEnd: number | undefined; // where this block should start if it follows the last: undefined while stopped
    let block: Block | null = null;
    const tick = (_t: number, off: number) => {
      block!.send("bytes", off, CLOCK);
    };
    return {
      process(b) {
        block = b;
        clock.begin(b);
        const t = clock.block;
        const playing = t.transport;

        // Re-arm on a fresh start, or on a ppqStart discontinuity while playing: a seek or loop needs a new locate,
        // and the arm gates risa's playback and discards the old position's queued clocks.
        const seek = ppqEnd !== undefined && Math.abs(t.ppqStart - ppqEnd) > RISA_SEEK_TOLERANCE;
        if (playing && (!prevT || seek)) {
          const loc = risaLocate(t.ppqStart);
          b.send("bytes", 0, risaArmPacket(loc), FLUSH); // F9 52 songRow chainRow tickOffset, flushing the FIFO
          b.send("bytes", 0, START);
          clock.next = loc.absoluteClock + 1; // risa primes the armed clock itself; we resume after it
        } else if (!playing && prevT) {
          b.send("bytes", 0, STOP);
        }

        if (playing) clock.walk(RISA_PPQN, tick); // F8 at 24 PPQN

        // Predict the next contiguous block's ppqStart for seek detection (the quarters this block spans).
        prevT = playing;
        if (playing) {
          const samplesPerQuarter = (t.sampleRate * 60) / t.tempo;
          ppqEnd = t.ppqStart + (samplesPerQuarter > 0 ? t.frames / samplesPerQuarter : 0);
        } else {
          ppqEnd = undefined;
        }
      },
    };
  },
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/smsSync.ts`:

````ts
// smsggdj's host sync (the `sms-sync` role's DSP behaviour, dspRoles.ts, as a script node): while the DAW plays, a
// 2-bit counter advanced one step a 24-PPQN tick, each step a LEVEL WORD at the tick's own frame, which the system
// holds on the sync lines until the next (smsSync.ts). `machine` picks which lines: controller port 2's TR + TH on a
// Master System, the EXT port's PC4/PC5 + PC6 on a Game Gear. No arm, no locate, no start or stop: the ROM reads
// deltas, and latches the lines itself when it arms.
//
// The role's glue, line for line, with its counter and its system's tick counter on the instance. A block allocates
// nothing.
import { bytes, defineNode, type Block } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import { s, type Infer } from "../../graph/settingsSchema";
import { SMS_SYNC_COUNTER_MOD, SMS_SYNC_PPQN, syncLevelsFor } from "../../smsSync";
import { TickClock } from "./clock";
import { CORE_BYTES } from "./ports";

export const SMS_SYNC_NODE_TYPE = "rp.sms.sync";

const settings = s.object({ machine: s.enum(["sms", "gg"], "sms") });

export type SmsSyncSettings = Infer<typeof settings>;

export const smsSyncNode = defineNode<SmsSyncSettings>({
  id: SMS_SYNC_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "smsggdj Host Sync",
  category: "protocol",
  settings,
  reshapes: true,
  ports: { bytes: bytes.out(CORE_BYTES) },
  create: ({ settings: initial }) => {
    let machine = initial.machine;
    const clock = new TickClock();
    // The counter is free-running and its absolute value is irrelevant (the ROM diffs it), so it is never reset, only
    // advanced. A walk advances `walking`, which becomes the counter once the walk is done, as the role kept it.
    let counter = 0;
    let walking = 0;
    let levels = syncLevelsFor(machine);
    let block: Block | null = null;
    const level = new Uint8Array(1);
    const tick = (_t: number, off: number) => {
      walking = (walking + 1) % SMS_SYNC_COUNTER_MOD;
      level[0] = levels(walking);
      block!.send("bytes", off, level);
    };
    return {
      process(b) {
        block = b;
        clock.begin(b);
        if (!clock.block.transport) return;
        levels = syncLevelsFor(machine);
        walking = counter;
        clock.walk(SMS_SYNC_PPQN, tick);
        counter = walking;
      },
      onSettings(next) {
        machine = next.machine;
      },
    };
  },
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/lsdjSync.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's sync (the `lsdj-sync` role's DSP behaviour, dspRoles.ts, as a script node): each block, the configured mode of
// LsdjSyncMode, the role's glue around the protocol's pure parts ported line for line. Its scratch is the role's one
// scratch bag, kept on the instance, so a mode change keeps what the role kept, and master sync's sub-object is dropped
// outside that mode as the role dropped it.
//
// What the modes read: the routed MIDI on `midi`, then the controller's launches on `launches`, as ONE inbox in that
// order, the order the kernel's inbox held them in (its launches appended at frame 0 after the routed events, so a
// frame merge would not be the same); and on `serialOut`, a feedback wire from the Game Boy's node, last block's
// captured serial-out bytes at their frames in that block, which MI.OUT and master sync decode.
//
// What they send: serial-in bytes, a run of same-frame bytes to a message as the kernel node sent them; a button
// press as [button, down] at frame 0; host MIDI out at frame 0. The frame-ordered queue raises a byte sent behind a
// later one (Arduinoboy's START after a row byte, MI.MAP's clocks after its rows) as it raised the kernel's.
//
// Nothing is allocated in a block but what the decoders allocate for the MIDI they emit, as under the kernel.
import { bytes, defineNode, events, type Block, type Message } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import { s, type Infer } from "../../graph/settingsSchema";
import { LSDJ_MODE_VALUES, LsdjSyncMode } from "../../settingsEnums";
import {
  KEYBOARD_LOW_OCTAVE_MAP,
  KEYBOARD_LOW_START,
  KEYBOARD_NOTE_MAP,
  KEYBOARD_NOTE_START,
  KEYBOARD_OCT_DN,
  KEYBOARD_OCT_UP,
  isExtendedScancode,
  toGbSerialByte,
} from "../../lsdjKeyboardMap";
import {
  arduinoboyDecodeSerialOut,
  arduinoboyMasterSyncBlock,
  type ArduinoboyState,
  type MasterSyncState,
} from "../../lsdjArduinoboy";
import {
  LSDJ_CLOCK,
  LSDJ_START,
  LSDJ_START_BUTTON,
  LSDJ_STOP,
  MIDIMAP_CLOCK,
  MIDIMAP_NOTEOFF,
  channelOf,
  isNoteOff,
  isNoteOn,
  midiMapRow,
} from "../../lsdjSyncBytes";
import { TickClock } from "./clock";
import { BUTTONS, MIDI_OUT, SERIAL_IN } from "./ports";

export const LSDJ_SYNC_NODE_TYPE = "rp.lsdj.sync";

// mode: LsdjSyncMode. tempoDivisor subdivides the 24-PPQN clock (24/divisor) for MidiSync, MidiSyncArduinoboy and
// MidiMap; the menu offers 1/2/4/8. autoStart taps START on the host transport's rise to auto-arm a SYNC=MIDI cart
// (MidiSync, MidiSyncArduinoboy), which a headless DAW render needs; off by default, so a cart arms by hand.
const settings = s.object({
  mode: s.enum(LSDJ_MODE_VALUES, "midiSync"),
  tempoDivisor: s.int({ min: 1, max: 8, default: 1 }),
  autoStart: s.bool(false),
});

export type LsdjSyncSettings = Infer<typeof settings>;

/** The role's scratch bag, every mode's fields in one, as the kernel kept it for the stage: a mode reads what another
 *  left (the Arduinoboy and MidiSync auto-arms share armDown) until a system is removed. The MI.OUT decoder keeps its
 *  own fields in it too. */
interface LsdjState extends ArduinoboyState {
  // MidiSyncArduinoboy
  playing?: boolean;
  divisor?: number;
  prevTransport?: boolean;
  armDown?: number;
  // MidiSync's auto-arm
  prevT?: boolean;
  // MidiMap
  lastRow?: number;
  // KeyboardMidi
  octave?: number;
  // MasterSync: dropped whenever the mode is not master sync, so coming back starts clean.
  masterSync?: MasterSyncState;
}

export const lsdjSyncNode = defineNode<LsdjSyncSettings>({
  id: LSDJ_SYNC_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "LSDj Sync",
  category: "protocol",
  settings,
  reshapes: true,
  ports: {
    midi: events.in(),
    launches: events.in(),
    serialOut: bytes.in(),
    serialIn: bytes.out(SERIAL_IN),
    buttons: events.out(BUTTONS),
    midiOut: events.out(MIDI_OUT),
  },
  create: ({ settings: initial }) => {
    let config = initial;
    const st: LsdjState = {};
    const clock = new TickClock();
    let block: Block | null = null; // the block being processed, which every send goes on
    let midi: readonly Message[] = [];
    let launches: readonly Message[] = [];
    // Last block's serial-out bytes, and each one's frame in that block, index for index: what the kernel handed a
    // stage as ctx.serialOut and ctx.serialOutFrames. Refilled each block, so they allocate nothing once grown.
    const serialOut: number[] = [];
    const serialOutFrames: number[] = [];
    const press = new Uint8Array(2);

    // The serial-in bytes not yet sent: consecutive bytes at runFrame, sent as one message when a byte at another
    // frame comes, and at the end of the block. Reused, so it allocates nothing once grown.
    const run: number[] = [];
    let runFrame = 0;
    const sendRun = () => {
      block!.send("serialIn", runFrame, run);
      run.length = 0;
    };
    const pushSerialIn = (frame: number, byte: number) => {
      if (run.length > 0 && frame !== runFrame) sendRun();
      runFrame = frame;
      run.push(byte & 0xff);
    };
    // At frame 0: the core takes a role's press with no frame.
    const pressButton = (button: number, down: boolean) => {
      press[0] = button;
      press[1] = down ? 1 : 0;
      block!.send("buttons", 0, press);
    };
    // Frame 0: MI.OUT and master sync carry no intra-block timing, and the host timestamps by block.
    const emitMidiOut = (data: number[]) => {
      block!.send("midiOut", 0, data);
    };
    // Each inbox event, through `handle`: the routed MIDI, then the launches.
    const eachEvent = (handle: (e: Message) => void) => {
      for (let i = 0; i < midi.length; i++) handle(midi[i]);
      for (let i = 0; i < launches.length; i++) handle(launches[i]);
    };

    // MidiSync's clock, at its tick's frame.
    const clockAtTick = (_t: number, off: number) => pushSerialIn(off, LSDJ_CLOCK);
    // MidiSyncArduinoboy's clock, at frame 0, NOT at its tick's frame. LSDj in Arduinoboy-slave mode toggles its
    // serial-clock-enable (SC) between bytes, so the SameBoy offset gate, which holds a byte until its frame, misses
    // LSDj's ready window and starves the clock (LSDj goes silent). The walk still sends the tempo-correct number of
    // clocks a block; only the intra-block time is dropped.
    const clockAtZero = () => pushSerialIn(0, LSDJ_CLOCK);
    // MidiMap's tick, at frame 0 for the same reason: Arduinoboy's Mode_LSDJ_Map turns each host 0xF8 into a 0xFF,
    // and LSDj advances one phrase step per 6 of them.
    const mapClockAtZero = () => pushSerialIn(0, MIDIMAP_CLOCK);

    // MidiSyncArduinoboy: notes drive runtime state. 24/25 toggle the play flag, 26-29 set the tempo divisor, 30 and
    // up push a raw row byte (note - 30).
    const arduinoboyEvent = (e: Message) => {
      if (!isNoteOn(e.data[0])) return;
      const note = e.data[1];
      if (note === 24) st.playing = true;
      else if (note === 25) st.playing = false;
      else if (note === 26) st.divisor = 1;
      else if (note === 27) st.divisor = 2;
      else if (note === 28) st.divisor = 4;
      else if (note === 29) st.divisor = 8;
      else if (note >= 30) pushSerialIn(e.frame, note - 30);
    };
    // MidiMap: a NoteOn is a row byte LSDj reads as a song-row jump; the NoteOff of the row last sounded sends the
    // 0xFE handshake.
    const midiMapEvent = (e: Message) => {
      const status = e.data[0];
      const note = e.data.length >= 2 ? e.data[1] : 0;
      if (isNoteOn(status)) {
        const row = midiMapRow(channelOf(status), note);
        if (row < 0) return;
        pushSerialIn(e.frame, row & 0xff);
        st.lastRow = row;
      } else if (isNoteOff(status)) {
        if (midiMapRow(channelOf(status), note) === st.lastRow) {
          pushSerialIn(e.frame, MIDIMAP_NOTEOFF);
          st.lastRow = -1;
        }
      }
    };
    // Slide LSDj's keyboard octave toward `target` with OCT_UP / OCT_DN scancodes; the new octave. Mirrors
    // slideKeyboardOctave in LsdjSyncRole.cpp.
    const slideKeyboardOctave = (frame: number, target: number, current: number): number => {
      if (target === current) return current;
      const code = toGbSerialByte(target > current ? KEYBOARD_OCT_UP : KEYBOARD_OCT_DN);
      let steps = Math.abs(target - current);
      while (steps-- > 0) pushSerialIn(frame, code);
      return target;
    };
    // KeyboardMidi: a NoteOn as LSDj's PS/2 scancodes, sliding the octave cursor to follow the note.
    const keyboardEvent = (e: Message) => {
      if (!isNoteOn(e.data[0])) return;
      let note = e.data[1];
      if (note >= KEYBOARD_NOTE_START) {
        note -= KEYBOARD_NOTE_START;
        st.octave = slideKeyboardOctave(e.frame, Math.floor(note / 12), st.octave!);
        const idx = note >= 0x3c ? (note % 12) + 0x0c : note % 12; // two rows of note keys
        pushSerialIn(e.frame, toGbSerialByte(KEYBOARD_NOTE_MAP[idx]));
      } else if (note >= KEYBOARD_LOW_START) {
        const command = KEYBOARD_LOW_OCTAVE_MAP[note - KEYBOARD_LOW_START];
        // Cursor keys need the extended (0xE0) prefix; every byte is mangled to LSDj's GB-serial form.
        if (isExtendedScancode(command)) pushSerialIn(e.frame, toGbSerialByte(0xe0));
        pushSerialIn(e.frame, toGbSerialByte(command));
      }
    };
    // MidiPassthrough: every byte verbatim.
    const passthroughEvent = (e: Message) => {
      const data = e.data;
      for (let j = 0; j < data.length; j++) pushSerialIn(e.frame, data[j]);
    };

    const dispatch = () => {
      const transport = clock.block.transport;
      // A mode's scratch survives a config change, so master sync's would go stale while another mode runs: dropped
      // here, coming back starts clean rather than from a stale run or a stale last byte.
      if (st.masterSync !== undefined && config.mode !== LsdjSyncMode.MasterSync) st.masterSync = undefined;
      switch (config.mode) {
        case LsdjSyncMode.MidiSync: {
          // Optional auto-arm: SYNC=MIDI LSDj follows the clock only once START has parked it in "wait for MIDI", so
          // tap START on the transport's rise (press for 2 blocks, then release).
          if (config.autoStart) {
            if (transport && !st.prevT) { pressButton(LSDJ_START_BUTTON, true); st.armDown = 2; }
            else if (st.armDown && st.armDown > 0) { if (--st.armDown === 0) pressButton(LSDJ_START_BUTTON, false); }
            st.prevT = transport;
          }
          const divisor = config.tempoDivisor || 1;
          clock.walk(24 / divisor, clockAtTick);
          break;
        }
        case LsdjSyncMode.MidiSyncArduinoboy: {
          if (st.divisor === undefined) st.divisor = config.tempoDivisor || 1;
          // autoStart: tap START on the host transport's rise to park a SYNC=Lsdj cart in "wait for sync" before the
          // note-24 play-enable and the clock arrive, so a headless render starts on the grid.
          if (config.autoStart) {
            if (transport && !(st.prevTransport ?? false)) { pressButton(LSDJ_START_BUTTON, true); st.armDown = 2; }
            else if (st.armDown && st.armDown > 0) { if (--st.armDown === 0) pressButton(LSDJ_START_BUTTON, false); }
          }
          eachEvent(arduinoboyEvent);
          if (transport !== (st.prevTransport ?? false)) {
            pushSerialIn(0, transport ? LSDJ_START : LSDJ_STOP);
            st.prevTransport = transport;
          }
          if (st.playing) clock.walk(24 / (st.divisor || 1), clockAtZero);
          break;
        }
        case LsdjSyncMode.MidiMap: {
          if (st.lastRow === undefined) st.lastRow = -1;
          eachEvent(midiMapEvent);
          // MI.MAP is a sync mode, so it clocks the cart too, transport-gated by the walk.
          const divisor = config.tempoDivisor || 1;
          clock.walk(24 / divisor, mapClockAtZero);
          break;
        }
        case LsdjSyncMode.KeyboardMidi:
          if (st.octave === undefined) st.octave = 4;
          eachEvent(keyboardEvent);
          break;
        case LsdjSyncMode.MidiPassthrough:
          eachEvent(passthroughEvent);
          break;
        case LsdjSyncMode.MidiOut: // ArduinoboyMaster / MIDIOUT: LSDj's MI.OUT stream, decoded to host MIDI
          if (serialOut.length > 0) arduinoboyDecodeSerialOut(serialOut, st, emitMidiOut);
          break;
        case LsdjSyncMode.MasterSync: // LSDj drives the host clock: a byte a clock, a silence the stop
          arduinoboyMasterSyncBlock(serialOut, serialOutFrames, clock.block, (st.masterSync ??= {}), emitMidiOut);
          break;
        default:
          break; // Off / Keyboard send nothing here
      }
    };

    return {
      // A throw goes to the script host, which counts it and runs this again next block: what was sent before it
      // stands, the held run included. A call the deadline stops skips the finally, so a run it left is cleared here
      // rather than sent in a block it was not pushed in.
      process(b) {
        block = b;
        run.length = 0;
        clock.begin(b);
        midi = b.messages("midi");
        launches = b.messages("launches");
        serialOut.length = 0;
        serialOutFrames.length = 0;
        const captured = b.messages("serialOut");
        for (let i = 0; i < captured.length; i++) {
          const m = captured[i];
          for (let j = 0; j < m.data.length; j++) {
            serialOut.push(m.data[j]);
            serialOutFrames.push(m.frame);
          }
        }
        try {
          dispatch();
        } finally {
          if (run.length > 0) sendRun();
        }
      },
      onSettings(next) {
        config = next;
      },
    };
  },
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/controllerSession.ts`:

````ts
// A control surface's session (the `launchpad` role's DSP behaviour, controllerRole.ts, as a script node): a
// ControllerSession (src/controller/session.ts) fed the surface's traffic and the block's clock each block, its LED
// bytes back to the device on `controllerOut`, its row launches onward: into the target system's lsdj-sync node on
// `launches`, or out of the host to a real Game Boy's Arduinoboy on `midiOut`, each at frame 0.
//
// Its settings are what the control plane resolved: the app's id, where its launches go and the system id they go
// to (the first system's when the user chose none), the app's config ALREADY PARSED by the app's own schema (the
// registry's, which this node never imports, so it carries no zod), the song's per-row timing table, and the start
// anchor. It parses nothing: the node imports only the apps' runtime (controller/apps/index.ts).
//
// The role's re-push rules, kept: a settings change whose shape (the app, the target, the system, the app's config)
// is the same adopts the new timing table in place, so the playhead does not move; any other rebuilds the session
// around the same predictor, so the song does not restart, and re-takes the device; an anchor is applied once per
// sequence number. As the role did, the work happens in the first process after the change.
//
// A block allocates nothing here beyond what the session does (its surface diff, and a launch's message).
import { control, defineNode, events, startValue, type Block } from "../../graph/defineNode";
import { s, type Infer } from "../../graph/settingsSchema";
import { CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES } from "../../settingsEnums";
import { ControllerSession } from "../../controller/session";
import { lsdjMidiMapTarget } from "../../controller/trackerTarget";
import { controllerApp } from "../../controller/apps";
// The leaf, not the lsdj/playback barrel: that also exports the observed model and the sav-derived table builder,
// which would pull the WRAM reader and the whole sav codec into the bundle.
import { PredictedLsdjModel, normaliseRowTicks } from "../../lsdj/playback/predict";
import { CONTROLLER_OUT, LAUNCHES, MIDI_OUT } from "./ports";

export const CONTROLLER_SESSION_NODE_TYPE = "rp.controller.session";

/** 24 PPQN, the resolution every Arduinoboy-family sync mode counts in. The session's tick is derived from ppq rather
 *  than counted: Math.floor(ppq * 24) is the quantity walkTicks derives its ticks from, so the session's clock and the
 *  cart's cannot drift apart, and a stopped transport freezes both. */
const TICKS_PER_QUARTER = 24;

const settings = s.object({
  /** Which controller app runs (an id in controller/apps/index.ts); an unknown one runs nothing. */
  app: s.string("lsdj-midimap"),
  target: s.enum(CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES, "system"),
  /** The system the launches are for, resolved: 0 is none. Where they go is the wiring's; the session is rebuilt
   *  when it changes, as it was for a new target. */
  systemId: s.int({ min: 0, max: 0xffffffff, default: 0 }),
  /** The app's own config, parsed by its schema on the control plane. */
  appConfig: s.json<Record<string, unknown>>({}),
  /** The per-row timing table (normaliseRowTicks reads it): the predictor's only input. */
  songRowTicks: s.json<unknown>([]),
  /** The start-edge re-anchor: where the cart said it was when the player started it themselves, and a sequence
   *  number so one anchor is applied once. Empty and 0 on the real-hardware path. */
  anchorRows: s.json<(number | null)[]>([]),
  anchorSeq: s.int({ min: 0, max: 0x7fffffff, default: 0 }),
});

export type ControllerSessionSettings = Infer<typeof settings>;

/** The settings that need a NEW session rather than an in-place update: which app runs, where its launches go, and
 *  the app's own knobs (an app reads some of those once into its state, so swapping the config underneath it would
 *  leave half the change applied). */
const shapeOf = (s: ControllerSessionSettings): string => JSON.stringify([s.app, s.target, s.systemId, s.appConfig]);

/** What the session keeps between blocks, as the role kept it in its scratch bag. */
interface SessionState {
  /** Undefined until the first block builds one; null when the settings name no app. */
  session?: ControllerSession | null;
  /** Whether a device was attached on the previous block: the edge that takes it. */
  attached?: boolean;
  /** The predictor, held here as well as inside the session so a rebuild carries it over. */
  model?: PredictedLsdjModel;
  /** The timing table the model holds, by identity: settings arrive as a fresh object on every change. */
  table?: unknown;
  shape?: string;
  /** The last anchor sequence applied. */
  anchorSeq?: number;
}

export const controllerSessionNode = defineNode<ControllerSessionSettings>({
  id: CONTROLLER_SESSION_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "Controller Session",
  category: "controller",
  settings,
  reshapes: true,
  ports: {
    controllerIn: events.in(),
    controllerConnected: control.in(),
    controllerOut: events.out(CONTROLLER_OUT),
    launches: events.out(LAUNCHES),
    midiOut: events.out(MIDI_OUT),
  },
  create: ({ settings: initial }) => {
    let config = initial;
    let shape = shapeOf(initial);
    const st: SessionState = {};
    let block: Block | null = null; // the block being processed, which a launch is sent on
    // This block's surface messages, as the views the block handed over: the session decodes them and keeps none.
    const input: Uint8Array[] = [];
    const toLaunches = (data: number[]) => {
      block!.send("launches", 0, data);
    };
    const toMidiOut = (data: number[]) => {
      block!.send("midiOut", 0, data);
    };

    // The session for these settings, or null when they name no app. The ONE difference between driving an emulated
    // cart and driving a real Game Boy is where `send` puts the bytes, so both carry the same launch stream.
    const build = (model: PredictedLsdjModel): ControllerSession | null => {
      const app = controllerApp(config.app);
      if (!app) return null;
      const send = config.target === "midiOut" ? toMidiOut : toLaunches;
      return new ControllerSession(app, { playback: model, target: lsdjMidiMapTarget(send), config: config.appConfig });
    };

    return {
      process(b) {
        block = b;
        // A re-push. A new timing table is adopted IN PLACE, so a chain added to row 12 lights up without the playhead
        // moving; anything structural rebuilds the session, carrying the predictor across so the song does not
        // restart.
        if (st.session === undefined || st.shape !== shape) {
          if (st.model) st.model.setRowTicks(config.songRowTicks); // carried over: the table may have moved too
          else st.model = PredictedLsdjModel.fromRowTicks(normaliseRowTicks(config.songRowTicks));
          st.session = build(st.model);
          st.shape = shape;
          st.table = config.songRowTicks;
          st.attached = false; // a fresh surface has no idea what the device is showing: re-take it below
        } else if (st.table !== config.songRowTicks) {
          st.model?.setRowTicks(config.songRowTicks);
          st.table = config.songRowTicks;
        }

        // Re-anchor when the control plane saw the cart start playing on its own, once per sequence number.
        const seq = config.anchorSeq ?? 0;
        if (seq !== st.anchorSeq) {
          st.anchorSeq = seq;
          if (seq > 0 && Array.isArray(config.anchorRows)) st.model?.anchorTo(config.anchorRows);
        }

        const session = st.session;
        if (!session) return; // an unknown app id: nothing to run

        // Take the device on the block a link first reports one: a device boots into Live mode, so Programmer mode
        // is entered every time one appears, and connect() invalidates the shadow buffer so the surface repaints.
        const attached = startValue(b.control("controllerConnected")) !== 0;
        if (attached && !st.attached) {
          const hello = session.connect();
          for (let i = 0; i < hello.length; i++) b.send("controllerOut", 0, hello[i]);
        }
        st.attached = attached;

        // Run even with nothing attached: update drives the predictor, so the LEDs are right the moment a device
        // appears. A surface's timing is not musical (the app quantises a press), so the frames are dropped.
        const messages = b.messages("controllerIn");
        input.length = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) input.push(messages[i].data);
        const out = session.update({
          input,
          tick: Math.floor(b.transport.ppq * TICKS_PER_QUARTER),
          transport: b.transport.playing,
        });
        for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i++) b.send("controllerOut", 0, out[i]);
      },
      onSettings(next) {
        config = next;
        shape = shapeOf(next);
      },
    };
  },
});
````

### Task 3: `rp.host.midi-out` takes each input's system from its settings, beside its prefixed form

Each protocol node has a `midiOut` of its own, so the host node must learn whose MIDI a message is from its wiring
rather than from the private 4-byte prefix the kernel node writes (design section 5). `{"systems": [id, ...]}` gives
it an events input per entry, `in1` to `inN` (1-based, as `rp.core.merge` spells its inputs), each holding one
producer's MIDI as it is: each block every input's messages go to the engine's host MIDI out under that entry's
system, input by input, each in queue order, never merged by frame, so the order a document wires its producers in is
the host's order across them. Two entries may name one system (a controller's launches to a real Game Boy, under the
id of a system whose own MI.OUT goes out too). Any 32-bit id is taken, 0 and 4294967295 included: the node tags, and
leaves to the document whether an id names one of its systems. At most 128 inputs (`kMidiOutMaxSystems`: a host MIDI
out producer for every system an engine holds, and a controller's, with room), since each commit copies the ids into
a fixed array, which must not allocate.

With no systems, `{}` or an empty list, it is the node it was: the one prefixed `midi` input the kernel node feeds,
until Task 6 deletes that form. Each form refuses the other's ports (`unknown-port`). The inputs are appended by
`adjust_layout`, none reflected; a wire carries its source's queue, so each input is sized at its producer. Its
prepare is stateless (`stateless_prepare`): a change of systems that keeps the inputs is a swap, and one that moves
them a rebuild, which loses nothing. This task comes before the equivalence rig, where design section 7 had it after:
the rig's per-role document needs it, since no protocol node writes the prefix. `NodeRig` now records the host MIDI
out and the drops a node reports.

````diff
 // The engine's host I/O nodes and the cart mirror (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md sections 3.3 to 3.5): what

+TEST_CASE("a change to rp.host.midi-out's systems replans cleanly, its inputs moved or kept", "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
+    // On an Engine, from the prefixed form to systems and back, rp.host.midi-in's output wired to every input: the
+    // engine's MIDI out is each input's messages in turn, under that input's system. A change that moves the inputs
+    // rebuilds the node and one that keeps them swaps its settings; either way the next block goes out as the new
+    // settings say, with nothing dropped and no fault.
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    const auto plan = [&](const std::string& settings, std::vector<std::string> inputs) {
+        std::vector<std::string> wires;
+        for (const auto& in : inputs) wires.push_back(docWire("midi-in.midi", "midi-out." + in));
+        return e.setGraph(hostIoOnly({docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), docNode("midi-out", "rp.host.midi-out", settings)},
+                                     std::move(wires)));
+    };
+    // Two messages staged out of frame order, which midi-in sorts.
+    const auto run = [&](bool prefixed) {
+        e.stageMidi(3, prefixed ? tagged(5, {0xF8}) : std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0xF8});
+        e.stageMidi(1, prefixed ? tagged(5, {0xFA}) : std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0xFA});
+        block(e);
+        return midiOut(e);
+    };
+    // Each system in turn: the two messages under it.
+    const auto under = [](std::vector<std::uint32_t> systems) {
+        std::vector<Out> out;
+        for (const auto s : systems) {
+            out.push_back({s, 1, {0xFA}});
+            out.push_back({s, 3, {0xF8}});
+        }
+        return out;
+    };
+
+    REQUIRE(plan("", {"midi"}).ok);
+    CHECK(run(true) == under({5}));
+    REQUIRE(plan(R"({"systems":[7,9,7]})", {"in1", "in2", "in3"}).ok);  // a rebuild: midi gone, in1 to in3 new
+    CHECK(run(false) == under({7, 9, 7}));
+    REQUIRE(plan(R"({"systems":[9]})", {"in1"}).ok);  // a rebuild: in2 and in3 gone
+    CHECK(run(false) == under({9}));
+    REQUIRE(plan(R"({"systems":[11]})", {"in1"}).ok);  // a swap: the same input, another system
+    CHECK(run(false) == under({11}));
+    REQUIRE(plan(R"({"systems":[11,12]})", {"in1", "in2"}).ok);
+    CHECK(run(false) == under({11, 12}));
+    REQUIRE(plan(R"({"systems":[]})", {"midi"}).ok);  // and back
+    CHECK(run(true) == under({5}));
+    CHECK(e.droppedMessages() == 0);
+    CHECK(e.faultCount() == 0);
+}
````

````bash
feat(engine): rp.host.midi-out takes each input's system from its settings, beside its prefixed form

{"systems": [id, ...]} gives the node an events input per entry, in1 to inN (rp.core.merge's spelling), each
holding one producer's MIDI unprefixed: each block every input's messages go to the engine's host MIDI out under
that entry's system, input by input, each in queue order, never merged by frame. Two entries may name one system.
With no systems, or an empty list, it is the node it was: the one `midi` input whose messages carry a 4-byte system
prefix, which the kernel node still feeds. The inputs are appended by adjust_layout (none reflected), copied into a
fixed array at each commit (at most kMidiOutMaxSystems, 128), sized by their producers since a wire carries its
source's queue, and a change that keeps them is a swap (stateless_prepare) where one that moves them rebuilds.

NodeRig now records the host MIDI out and the drops. HostIo.test.cpp holds the systems form input by input under
each input's id (a repeated id, frames, order, short and empty messages kept), the prefixed form under every spelling
of none, each form refusing the other's ports, a replan through prefixed -> systems -> fewer -> swapped -> more ->
prefixed on an Engine, and the settings' bounds.
EOF
````

---

### Task 4: The kernel node's recorded digests, held by the per-role graph too

`KernelNode.test.cpp` holds the kernel node to digests recorded while the old native kernel stage ran beside it: per
block, each system's four inputs in structure order (`serialIn` byte by byte), then the host MIDI out and the
control-surface out. A digest hashes what reaches each system input and the host, not which node sent it, so the
same cases run on the per-role graph must give the same values: B3b's bit-for-bit proof of the nodes, independent of
parity (design section 6, "Equivalence").

Every case becomes a `TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE` over two graphs, `KernelGraph` and `PerRoleGraph`, held to the same
recorded values and the same finish checks. `perRoleDocument()` builds what B3b's `buildGraph` is to place, between
the same host I/O nodes, feeds and probes: `rp.host.midi-in` into `routing` (the routing role's mode, the system ids
in slot order); a `controller` session when the structure has a launchpad, its target 0 resolved to the first
system's id and its app config parsed with its defaults; each system's protocol nodes, `sys-<id>/<kind>` in slot
order with store-parsed configs, each output into the probe the kernel's `sys-<id>.*` output went to; a Game Boy's
MI.OUT feed into its `rp.lsdj.sync`'s `serialOut` only; the controller's launches only into a "system" target's
`rp.lsdj.sync`; and `rp.host.midi-out` in its systems form, the controller's `midiOut` into `in1` and each
`rp.lsdj.sync`'s after it in slot order (with no producer, `{"systems":[]}` left unwired). A structure change checks,
on either graph, that every node placed before and after keeps its instance and that the instances alive are the
nodes placed, so a re-added system's nodes are new.

Every recorded value held on the per-role graph, with no node needing a fix, but one block of the throw case, which
differs by design: a throw now stops only the node it is in, so the third system's mGB forwards its MIDI in the block
where the second system's LSDj throws. That block's digest takes the third system as the kernel left it
(`unsentByKernel`), and the case checks what the per-role graph sent instead. One case is added, recorded from the
kernel node: a controller with its default target launching at once behind routed MIDI into an MI.MAP cart, then its
host MIDI out ahead of two Game Boys' in the same blocks. Design section 5's items 2, 3 and 6 (host MIDI out's order
across nodes, launches after routed events, the controller's default target) were orders no earlier case sent a
message through, so without it the rig could not catch a change in them.

````diff
+std::vector<std::string> perRoleNodes(const Structure& s) {
+    std::vector<std::string> ids{"routing"};

+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < wires.size(); ++i) doc += (i ? "," : "") + wires[i];
````

````bash
digest takes the third system as the kernel left it, and the case checks what the per-role graph sent instead.
````

---

### Task 5: The flip - the kernel dissolved into the graph

Production runs the per-role graph (design section 4): `buildGraph` places the routing, the controller and a
protocol node per role instead of the kernel node, `kernelProjection`'s special cases folded in, and the stores
publish what it needs. One change, accepted by strict parity: every file bit for bit, nothing re-recorded. The kernel
node stays registered, unplaced, until Task 6 deletes it.

- **The model.** `GraphModel` loses the kernel's project stages and gains `midiRouting` (absent or null places no
  routing node, as a `DirectGraph` or a lone `SystemsStore` publishes until a mode is set) and `controller`, a
  `GraphController`: its app, target and configured `systemId` (0 is the first system), its app config already
  parsed, the timing table, the anchor, and the cart's own SYNC as last polled. Each system's `pipeline` holds the
  roles that have a protocol node, each a `ProtocolRole`: its kind, the node type it is placed as, and its config as
  the store parsed it (a node's settings fill their defaults where the kernel's roles read a missing field as nothing,
  so the configs must be parsed).
- **The table.** Which role kind is placed as which node, and how each type is wired (the input its routed MIDI
  arrives on, the system inputs it writes, whether it takes launches, serial out or sends host MIDI), is
  `graph/protocolNodes.ts`: pure, zod-free and registry-free, so both stores and a `DirectGraph` read it with or without
  a registry. A `node` field on `RoleType` would have needed it as a fallback anyway: two sources that could disagree.
  `protocolNodeOf` replaces the stores' `isSystemStage` / `runsInKernel`; `test/system-settings/registry.test.ts`
  holds the table to the registry's roles `isSystemStage` passes, and `build-graph.test.ts` its type ids to the node
  modules' own (importing them would pull every protocol into whatever imports `buildGraph`).
- **The document.** In order: `midi-in`, `controller-in`, `routing`, `controller`, each system's protocol nodes
  (`sys-<id>/<kind>`, slot order then pipeline order), the systems (in sum order, as before), the cart mirror,
  `midi-out`, `controller-out`, then the audio. The routed MIDI goes into each node that reads it, the controller's
  launches only into a "system" target's `rp.lsdj.sync`, each node's outputs into its system's inputs of the same
  name, a Game Boy's `serialOut` back only into its `rp.lsdj.sync` (a feedback wire, as before), the N8 cart mirror
  from the first NES's `rp.n8.midi-to-fifo.midi` and `rp.risa.sync.bytes`, and `rp.host.midi-out` in its systems
  form, the controller first (under its resolved target), then each `rp.lsdj.sync` in slot order. With no producer
  it is placed with `{"systems":[]}`, which until Task 6 is its prefixed form, left unwired.
- **The controller.** `graph/controller.ts` holds what `kernelProjection` did besides: the target resolved at each
  publish ("0 is the first system"; with no systems its host MIDI is tagged 4294967295, the kernel's -1, `NO_SYSTEM`),
  the MI.MAP override written into the target cart's `rp.lsdj.sync` settings alone (so nothing reaches the `.rplg`,
  and the controller menu reads the same helper), and the node's settings. The app config is parsed by the publisher,
  through `parseAppConfig(id, raw)` in `controller/registry.ts` (an id no app has gets `{}`): `buildGraph` stays pure
  and registry-free. `kernelProjection.ts` goes, its tests moving to `buildGraph`'s, the store's and the config's.
- **The publishers.** `ProjectStore.publishGraph` publishes `{ systems, routing, midiRouting, controller }`, the
  controller from `controllerModel()`; `SystemsStore.graphSystems` hands each system's protocol pipeline;
  `DirectGraph` keeps `setPipeline` and `setProjectStages` (mapped onto the new model, the routing before the
  controller whatever order the stages come in) and gains `setMidiRouting` and `setController`.
- **The planner's order.** The planner keeps document order among nodes ready at once (`Planner.cpp` `order()`
  takes the lowest document index among the ready groups), so every script node runs before the systems, and the
  profile build's `apu-render` span, which begins where the last script node's `process` ended, needs no change; its
  comment now says why.
- **The goldens.** The 840 `buildGraph` goldens are re-recorded by a one-off script: every model routes send-to-all,
  with no controller and no roles, so each document places the routing node and no protocol node, and the audio of
  every one of the 238 documents is as it was. The native golden runner still plans and runs every document with no
  fault, throw or drop.

Behaviour that changes where no parity case looks, besides Task 2's list: a `DirectGraph`'s controller gets the MI.MAP
override a project's does; an input or host I/O node with nothing to feed it is left unwired, where the kernel's
outputs were wired and sent nothing. spec/03 and spec/04 describe the store-to-graph seam (Task 8 rewrites the rest).

**Files:** 37 files, by step below.
- Create: `packages/retroplug/src/graph/controller.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/graph/protocolNodes.ts`
- Delete: `packages/retroplug/src/kernelProjection.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/dsp/projection.test.ts`
- Modify: 33 files

````diff
+  expect(gone.document.wires.some((w) => w.from === "controller.launches")).toBe(false);
+  expect(gone.node("controller")?.settings?.systemId).toBe(9);
+});

+test("host MIDI out takes the controller's first, then each lsdj-sync node's in slot order, each under its system", () => {
+  const g = built([gb(3, 1, [LSDJ("midiOut")]), gb(1, 0, [MGB]), gb(2, 1, [LSDJ("masterSync")])], "stereo", multi(2), withController({ systemId: 2 }));
+  expect(g.node("midi-out")?.settings).toEqual({ systems: [2, 3, 2] });
+  expect([1, 2, 3].map((k) => g.into(`midi-out.in${k}`))).toEqual([["controller.midiOut"], ["sys-3/lsdj-sync.midiOut"], ["sys-2/lsdj-sync.midiOut"]]);
+  // With no system to resolve "the first" to, the controller's is tagged as the kernel tagged it (its -1), and the node
+  // takes 0, its none.
+  const empty = built([], "stereo", multi(2), withController());
+  expect(empty.node("midi-out")?.settings).toEqual({ systems: [0xffffffff] });
+  expect(empty.node("controller")?.settings?.systemId).toBe(0);
+  // Nothing that sends host MIDI: an input for nothing.
+  expect(built([gb(1, 0, [MGB])]).node("midi-out")?.settings).toEqual({ systems: [] });
+});
+
+test("the cart mirrors the first NES in slot order, fed what its protocol nodes feed it, and there is no mirror without a NES", () => {
+  const g = built([gb(1), nes(9, 0, [N8, RISA]), nes(3, 0, [N8])]);
   expect(g.node("cart")).toEqual({ id: "cart", type: "rp.n8.cart-mirror", settings: { system: 9 } });
-  expect(g.from("cart.midi")).toBe("kernel.sys-9.midi");
-  expect(g.from("cart.bytes")).toBe("kernel.sys-9.bytes");
+  expect(g.into("cart.midi")).toEqual(["sys-9/nes-n8-midi.midi"]);
+  expect(g.into("cart.bytes")).toEqual(["sys-9/risa-sync.bytes"]);
+  // A NES with no risa-sync sends its cart no bytes; one with no protocol node at all, nothing.
+  expect(built([nes(4, 0, [N8])]).into("cart.bytes")).toEqual([]);
+  expect(built([nes(4)]).document.wires.some((w) => w.to.startsWith("cart."))).toBe(false);
   expect(built([gb(1), gb(2)]).node("cart")).toBe(undefined);
   expect(built([]).node("cart")).toBe(undefined);
 });
+
+// --- the cart's sync mode under a controller ----------------------------------------------------------------
+//
+// The two settings have to agree and nothing made them. `lsdj-sync` defaults to `midiSync`, while the MI.MAP app's
+// launches are NoteOns that only the `midiMap` translator turns into row bytes - so enabling a Launchpad on a fresh
+// cart clocked it for a mode it was not in, sent launches nowhere, and left LSDj sitting on "WAIT". Reported from a
+// hardware session. The document forces it in that cart's lsdj-sync node alone, so nothing reaches the `.rplg`.
+
+const syncModeOf = (g: ReturnType<typeof built>, id: number): unknown => g.node(`sys-${id}/lsdj-sync`)?.settings?.mode;
+
+test("an enabled controller drives its cart in MI.MAP, whatever the stored mode said", () => {
+  const g = built([gb(1, 0, [LSDJ()])], "stereo", multi(2), withController({ cartSync: "MidiMap" }));
+  expect(syncModeOf(g, 1)).toBe("midiMap");
+  expect(g.node("sys-1/lsdj-sync")?.settings).toEqual({ mode: "midiMap", tempoDivisor: 1, autoStart: false });
+});
+
+test("systemId 0 means the first system, matching what the node resolves", () => {
+  const g = built([gb(7, 0, [LSDJ()]), gb(8, 0, [LSDJ()])], "stereo", multi(2), withController({ systemId: 0 }));
+  expect(syncModeOf(g, 7)).toBe("midiMap");
+  expect(syncModeOf(g, 8)).toBe("midiSync"); // a peer cart is left entirely alone
+});
+
+test("a cart in some OTHER sync mode is not driven at all", () => {
+  // Not politeness: a cart in LSDJ (master) mode drives the link itself, so our clock bytes collide with
+  // its own and LSDj reports TOO BUSY and stops rendering properly.
+  expect(syncModeOf(built([gb(1, 0, [LSDJ()])], "stereo", multi(2), withController({ cartSync: "Lsdj" })), 1)).toBe("off");
+});
+
+test("an unread battery is assumed willing rather than refused", () => {
+  // The case on a freshly built system whose battery has not been published yet.
+  expect(syncModeOf(built([gb(1, 0, [LSDJ()])], "stereo", multi(2), withController({ cartSync: null })), 1)).toBe("midiMap");
+});
+
+test("nothing is overridden without a controller, or when it drives real hardware, or for another app", () => {
+  expect(syncModeOf(built([gb(1, 0, [LSDJ()])]), 1)).toBe("midiSync");
+  // target midiOut is the real-Game-Boy path: there is no emulated cart to configure, and the emulated one
+  // sitting in the project is somebody else's.
+  expect(syncModeOf(built([gb(1, 0, [LSDJ()])], "stereo", multi(2), withController({ target: "midiOut" })), 1)).toBe("midiSync");
+  expect(syncModeOf(built([gb(1, 0, [LSDJ()])], "stereo", multi(2), withController({ app: "another" })), 1)).toBe("midiSync");
+  expect(controllerSyncOverride([], CONTROLLER)).toBe(null); // no cart to drive
+});
+
+test("the override leaves the model's own pipeline as it was", () => {
+  // The whole reason it happens in the document: turning the controller off restores whatever the user had.
+  const systems = [gb(1, 0, [LSDJ()])];
+  expect(syncModeOf(built(systems, "stereo", multi(2), withController({ cartSync: "MidiMap" })), 1)).toBe("midiMap");
+  expect(systems[0].pipeline[0].config.mode).toBe("midiSync");
+  expect(syncModeOf(built(systems), 1)).toBe("midiSync");
+});

+
+// --- the controller ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Only the user's choices persist. The graph's controller node carries a ~1000-number timing table derived from the
+// cart's battery, and being synthesized at each publish is what keeps that out of the `.rplg`.
+
+test("the derived song table never reaches a saved project", () => {
+  // A `.rplg` holds the user's CHOICES; a thousand numbers re-derivable from the cart's own battery would be derived
+  // data in a config file, and stale the moment the song changed.
+  const settings = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, controller: { enabled: true, app: "lsdj-midimap", target: "system" as const, systemId: 0, appConfig: { quantise: "bar" } } };
+  const json = serializeConfig(buildConfig(settings, []), "", identity);
+
+  expect(json.includes("songRowTicks")).toBe(false);
+  expect(json.includes("launchpad")).toBe(false);
+  expect(parseConfig(json).settings.controller.enabled).toBe(true); // but the choice itself persists
+  expect(parseConfig(json).settings.controller.appConfig).toEqual({ quantise: "bar" });
+});
+
+test("an older project with no controller key loads with it defaulted off, needing no migration", () => {
+  const raw = JSON.stringify({ schemaVersion: K_PROJECT, settings: { layout: "auto", midiRouting: "sendToAll", audioRouting: "stereo", zoom: 0 }, systems: [] });
+  expect(parseConfig(raw).settings.controller).toEqual({ enabled: false, app: "lsdj-midimap", target: "system", systemId: 0, appConfig: {} });
+});

+test("the protocol-node table names a node for exactly the app's roles the DSP kernel ran per system", () => {
+  // The stores place what graph/protocolNodes.ts says, not what a registry says, so the two must agree for every
+  // role the app registers: every kind the kernel ran as a system stage has a node, and no other kind does.
+  const kinds: string[] = [];
+  const register = RoleRegistry.prototype.registerRole;
+  RoleRegistry.prototype.registerRole = function (t) {
+    kinds.push(t.kind);
+    register.call(this, t);
+  };
+  let registry: RoleRegistry;
+  try {
+    registry = buildAppRegistry();
+  } finally {
+    RoleRegistry.prototype.registerRole = register;
+  }
+  expect(kinds.length).toBeGreaterThan(10);
+  for (const kind of kinds) expect(protocolNodeOf(kind) !== undefined, kind).toBe(isSystemStage(registry.roleType(kind)));
+});
````

````ts
// The protocol nodes a system's roles are placed as (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md section 2): which role
// kind has a script node, its type, and how buildGraph wires each type between the routing, the controller, its
// system and the host. Pure and zod-free, so buildGraph, both stores and a DirectGraph read the same table, with or
// without a role registry.
//
// The mapping lives here rather than on RoleType because the node types are code in the script-node bundle every
// Engine embeds: which role kinds have one is a fact of that bundle, not of whichever registry a store was handed,
// and three publishers need it, two of which hold no registry at all (a DirectGraph, a SystemsStore built without
// one, as the tests build them). A field on RoleType would need this table as its fallback anyway, which makes two
// sources that can disagree about a role. The registry stays what it is to the app: each role's schema,
// onConstruct and menu, on the control plane.
import type { RoleInstance } from "../systemRoles";

/** The system-node inputs a protocol node feeds, each from its output of the same name. */
export type SystemInput = "serialIn" | "midi" | "bytes" | "buttons";

/** How buildGraph wires a protocol node type. */
export interface ProtocolNodeSpec {
  /** The input its system's routed MIDI arrives on, or null for a node that reads only the transport. */
  midiIn: string | null;
  /** The system inputs it writes. No two roles of one system write the same one, so no input is fed twice. */
  writes: readonly SystemInput[];
  /** It takes the controller's launches on `launches` when its system is the controller's target. */
  launches?: true;
  /** It takes its Game Boy's serial out on `serialOut`, a block late (a feedback wire): what MI.OUT and master sync
   *  decode. */
  serialOut?: true;
  /** It sends host MIDI on `midiOut`, under its system's id. */
  midiOut?: true;
}

// Each type's id as its node module spells it (script/nodes/*.ts), which test/graph/build-graph.test.ts holds these
// to: importing the modules would pull every protocol into whatever imports buildGraph.
export const PROTOCOL_NODES = {
  "rp.mgb.midi": { midiIn: "midi", writes: ["serialIn"] },
  "rp.n8.midi-to-fifo": { midiIn: "midiIn", writes: ["midi"] },
  "rp.risa.sync": { midiIn: null, writes: ["bytes"] },
  "rp.sms.sync": { midiIn: null, writes: ["bytes"] },
  "rp.lsdj.sync": { midiIn: "midi", writes: ["serialIn", "buttons"], launches: true, serialOut: true, midiOut: true },
} as const satisfies Record<string, ProtocolNodeSpec>;

export type ProtocolNodeType = keyof typeof PROTOCOL_NODES;

/** The role kinds whose DSP behaviour the kernel ran for a system, each with the node type it is placed as. */
const ROLE_NODES: Readonly<Record<string, ProtocolNodeType>> = {
  mgb: "rp.mgb.midi",
  "nes-n8-midi": "rp.n8.midi-to-fifo",
  "risa-sync": "rp.risa.sync",
  "sms-sync": "rp.sms.sync",
  "lsdj-sync": "rp.lsdj.sync",
};

/** A role on a system as buildGraph places it: its node, `sys-<id>/<kind>`, of type `node`, with the role's config as
 *  the store parsed it as its settings. */
export interface ProtocolRole {
  kind: string;
  node: ProtocolNodeType;
  config: Record<string, unknown>;
}

/** The node type a role of `kind` is placed as, or undefined for a role with none: a core's config role, and the
 *  features with no DSP behaviour (asset overrides, a ROM's facts). */
export function protocolNodeOf(kind: string): ProtocolNodeType | undefined {
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ROLE_NODES, kind) ? ROLE_NODES[kind] : undefined;
}

/** `roles`, in order, as the protocol nodes they are placed as; a role with none is left out, so an edit to it (a
 *  model, a palette, an asset override) leaves the document as it was. */
export function protocolPipeline(roles: readonly RoleInstance[]): ProtocolRole[] {
  const out: ProtocolRole[] = [];
  for (const r of roles) {
    const node = protocolNodeOf(r.kind);
    if (node) out.push({ kind: r.kind, node, config: r.config });
  }
  return out;
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/graph/controller.ts`:

````ts
// A control-surface session as buildGraph places it (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md section 4): what the
// control plane hands it, the system its launches are for, and the lsdj-sync mode the cart it drives must be in.
// Pure and registry-free: the publisher (ProjectStore, or a DirectGraph) parses the app's config with the app's own
// schema before it gets here, so neither buildGraph nor the node it places imports a zod schema.
import type { ControllerTarget } from "../settingsEnums";
import type { RowTicksTable } from "../lsdj/playback/predict";
import type { ControllerAnchor } from "../lsdj/playback/anchor";

/** An enabled controller: the user's choices, and what the control plane derived for it. */
export interface GraphController {
  /** Which controller app runs (controller/apps); an id no app has runs nothing. */
  app: string;
  /** Where its launches go: into the target cart's lsdj-sync node ("system"), or out of the host to a real Game
   *  Boy's Arduinoboy ("midiOut"). */
  target: ControllerTarget;
  /** The system they are for, as the user chose it: 0 is the first system. */
  systemId: number;
  /** The app's own config, already parsed by the app's schema (controller/registry.ts parseAppConfig). */
  appConfig: Record<string, unknown>;
  /** The per-row timing table the predictor runs on, derived from the cart's battery. Never persisted: it rides the
   *  document, so a synthesized node is what carries it rather than the `.rplg`. */
  songRowTicks: RowTicksTable;
  /** Where the cart was seen starting on its own, or null on the hardware path / before it ever has. */
  anchor: ControllerAnchor | null;
  /** The cart's OWN SYNC setting, as last polled ("MidiMap", "Lsdj", ...), or null when unreadable. */
  cartSync: string | null;
}

/** The system a controller's host MIDI is tagged with when there is no system to resolve "the first" to: the
 *  kernel's -1, as the unsigned id rp.host.midi-out carries. */
export const NO_SYSTEM = 0xffffffff;

/** The system a controller's launches are for: the chosen one, else the first system, else NO_SYSTEM. An id that
 *  names no live system is left as it is, so its launches go nowhere rather than into whichever cart is first. */
export function controllerTarget(
  controller: Pick<GraphController, "systemId">,
  systems: readonly { id: number }[],
): number {
  if (controller.systemId > 0) return controller.systemId;
  return systems.length > 0 ? systems[0].id : NO_SYSTEM;
}

/** The `lsdj-sync` mode the controller needs the cart it drives to be in, and which system that is.
 *  Null when no controller is driving an emulated cart.
 *
 *  This exists because the two settings MUST agree and nothing made them. `lsdj-sync` defaults to
 *  `midiSync`, while the MI.MAP app's launches are NoteOns that only the `midiMap` translator turns into
 *  row bytes - so enabling a Launchpad on a fresh cart produced a cart being clocked for a mode it was not
 *  in, launches that went nowhere, and LSDj sitting on "WAIT". Reported from a hardware session.
 *
 *  The override is applied to the document, to that cart's lsdj-sync node's settings alone, rather than written
 *  into the project, which is what makes it safe: nothing reaches the `.rplg`, and turning the controller off
 *  restores whatever the user had.
 *
 *  `off` when the CART's own SYNC says it is not in MI.MAP. That is not politeness - a cart in LSDJ (master)
 *  mode drives the link itself, so our clock bytes collide with its own and LSDj reports TOO BUSY and stops
 *  rendering properly. Measured in test-native/lsdj-sync-toggle. Better to send a cart that is not listening
 *  nothing at all. */
export function controllerSyncOverride(
  systems: readonly { id: number }[],
  controller: Pick<GraphController, "app" | "target" | "systemId" | "cartSync"> | null | undefined,
): { systemId: number; mode: "midiMap" | "off" } | null {
  if (!controller || controller.target !== "system" || controller.app !== "lsdj-midimap") return null;
  const systemId = controllerTarget(controller, systems);
  if (systemId === NO_SYSTEM) return null;
  // A cart we cannot read is assumed willing: that is the case on a freshly built system whose battery has
  // not been published yet, and refusing to drive it would be a worse guess than trying.
  const mode = controller.cartSync && controller.cartSync !== "MidiMap" ? "off" : "midiMap";
  return { systemId, mode };
}

/** The controller node's settings (script/nodes/controllerSession.ts): its system resolved (0 is the node's none),
 *  and the anchor spelt as the node takes it. */
export function controllerSettings(controller: GraphController, target: number): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    app: controller.app,
    target: controller.target,
    systemId: target === NO_SYSTEM ? 0 : target,
    appConfig: controller.appConfig,
    songRowTicks: controller.songRowTicks,
    // The node re-anchors when the SEQ changes, so an anchor riding along on later publishes is applied once
    // rather than yanking the playhead back on every unrelated structure edit.
    anchorRows: controller.anchor?.rows ?? [],
    anchorSeq: controller.anchor?.seq ?? 0,
  };
}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: Re-record the 840 `buildGraph` goldens**

The documents change on purpose. The goldens file has no update mode, so the prototype re-recorded it with a
one-off script: each case's model loses the kernel's project stages (every golden's is empty) and gains the MIDI
routing a project publishes by default (send-to-all) and no controller; its systems keep their pipelines (every
golden's is empty, so no protocol node is placed). Each document is rebuilt, the distinct documents are re-indexed in
first-appearance order, and the script stops if any case's slots or tap arm move. First keep the old file for the
check that follows:

Run: `mkdir -p /tmp/b3bproto/stage5 && cp packages/retroplug/test/graph/golden/build-graph.json /tmp/b3bproto/stage5/build-graph.before.json`
Expected: nothing printed.

Save the script as `/tmp/b3bproto/stage5/regolden.ts` (from that directory its imports reach this worktree, `/workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish`):

````ts
// Re-record test/graph/golden/build-graph.json from buildGraph for the B3b flip: each case's model loses the kernel's
// `project` stages (every golden's is empty) and gains the MIDI routing a project publishes by default (send-to-all)
// and no controller; its systems keep their pipelines (every golden's is empty, so no protocol node is placed). Its
// document is rebuilt, and the distinct documents are re-indexed in first-appearance order. Slots and tap arms must
// not move.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { buildGraph } from "../../../workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph";
import { canonicalJson } from "../../../workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/retroplug/src/graph/canonicalJson";

const path = process.argv[2];
const golden = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
const docs: string[] = [];
const index = new Map<string, number>();
const cases = golden.cases.map((c: any) => {
  const { project, ...rest } = c.model;
  if (canonicalJson(project) !== "[]") throw new Error(`${c.name}: project stages were not empty`);
  if (c.model.systems.some((s: any) => canonicalJson(s.pipeline) !== "[]")) throw new Error(`${c.name}: a pipeline was not empty`);
  const model = { ...rest, midiRouting: "sendToAll", controller: null };
  const built = buildGraph(model);
  if (canonicalJson(built.slots) !== canonicalJson(c.slots)) throw new Error(`${c.name}: slots moved`);
  if (canonicalJson(built.tapArm) !== canonicalJson(c.tapArm)) throw new Error(`${c.name}: tapArm moved`);
  const text = canonicalJson(built.document);
  let at = index.get(text);
  if (at === undefined) {
    at = docs.length;
    docs.push(text);
    index.set(text, at);
  }
  return canonicalJson({ ...c, model, document: at });
});
writeFileSync(path, `{"documents":[\n${docs.join(",\n")}\n],"cases":[\n${cases.join(",\n")}\n]}\n`);
console.log(`${cases.length} cases, ${docs.length} documents (was ${golden.documents.length})`);
````

Run: `node_modules/.bin/esbuild /tmp/b3bproto/stage5/regolden.ts --bundle --platform=node --outfile=/tmp/b3bproto/stage5/regolden.js --log-level=warning && node /tmp/b3bproto/stage5/regolden.js packages/retroplug/test/graph/golden/build-graph.json`
Expected: `840 cases, 238 documents (was 238)`.

Then check that only what is around the audio moved, that the routing lists the systems in slot order, and that the kernel is gone. Save as `/tmp/b3bproto/stage5/check_goldens.py`:

````python
# Check the B3b re-record: only what is around the audio moved, the routing lists the systems in slot order, and the
# kernel is gone (no golden system has a role, so no protocol node, controller or host MIDI out input is placed).
import json
old=json.load(open('/tmp/b3bproto/stage5/build-graph.before.json'))
new=json.load(open('/workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/retroplug/test/graph/golden/build-graph.json'))
AROUND={"midi-in","controller-in","kernel","routing","controller","cart","midi-out","controller-out"}
def around(nid): return nid in AROUND or '/' in nid
def audio(doc):
    nodes=[n for n in doc['nodes'] if not around(n['id'])]
    def touches(e): return around(e.split('.',1)[0])
    wires=[w for w in doc['wires'] if not touches(w['from']) and not touches(w['to'])]
    return json.dumps({'nodes':nodes,'wires':wires}, sort_keys=True)
bad=0
for co,cn in zip(old['cases'],new['cases']):
    assert co['name']==cn['name']
    assert co['slots']==cn['slots'] and co['tapArm']==cn['tapArm'], cn['name']
    doc=new['documents'][cn['document']]
    if audio(old['documents'][co['document']])!=audio(doc): bad+=1; print('differs', co['name'])
    ids=[n['id'] for n in doc['nodes']]
    assert 'kernel' not in ids and 'controller' not in ids and not any('/' in i for i in ids), cn['name']
    r=[n for n in doc['nodes'] if n['id']=='routing'][0]
    assert r['settings']=={'mode':'sendToAll','systems':cn['slots']}, cn['name']
    assert [n for n in doc['nodes'] if n['id']=='midi-out'][0]['settings']=={'systems':[]}, cn['name']
    # Around the audio, only the routing's input: no system input, cart input or host output is fed.
    extra=[w for w in doc['wires'] if around(w['from'].split('.',1)[0]) or around(w['to'].split('.',1)[0])]
    assert extra==[{'from':'midi-in.midi','to':'routing.midiIn'}], (cn['name'], extra)
    # Script nodes before the systems, the host inputs first.
    assert ids[:3]==['midi-in','controller-in','routing'], cn['name']
print('cases', len(new['cases']), 'audio differs in', bad)
````

````diff
-## `kernelProjection` — store → kernel
-
-[projectKernelStructure(views, midiRouting, controller?)](../packages/retroplug/src/kernelProjection.ts#L72)
-is the single seam that turns "what the app has" into "what the DSP runs". Its `views` are
-`ProjectedSystem`s (`{ id, roles }`) in slot order:
-
-- each system's `roles` map straight into its `pipeline`, order preserved;
-- the project-scope `{ kind: "midi-routing", config: { mode: midiRouting } }` role is **synthesized**
-  from the project's MIDI-routing setting (it lives in project settings, not on any system);
-- with a controller enabled, the project-scope `launchpad` role is synthesized from the controller
-  settings the same way (its config carries the derived song-timing table, so it never reaches the
-  `.rplg`), and the `lsdj-sync` stage of the cart the MI.MAP app drives is forced to `midiMap`, or to
-  `off` when the cart's own SYNC setting is not MI.MAP (`controllerSyncOverride`).
-
-It is pure and **registry-free**: the kernel self-guards scope. `ProjectStore.publishGraph` calls it
-with each system's pipeline (`SystemsStore.graphSystems`: the roles the kernel runs, or every role for a
-store without a registry) and
-publishes the result with the graph, where `buildGraph` makes it the kernel node's settings, so every
-structural edit, and every edit to a role or setting the structure reads, reaches the kernel.
````

````bash
and the controller (its app, target and configured system, its app config parsed on the control plane by the app's
schema, the timing table, the anchor, and the cart's own SYNC as last polled). Each system's pipeline holds the
roles that have a protocol node, each with the node type it is placed as and its config as the store parsed it.

system's protocol nodes in slot order (sys-<id>/<kind>), the MI.MAP override written into the target cart's

form: the controller first, then each lsdj-sync in slot order ({"systems":[]} with none).

graph/controller.ts, where the controller menu reads it too. DirectGraph keeps setPipeline and setProjectStages,

ready at once, so every script node still runs before the systems, which the profile build's apu-render span
relies on.

The buildGraph goldens are re-recorded (every model routes send-to-all, with no controller and no roles; the audio
of all 840 documents is unchanged), and kernelProjection's tests move to buildGraph's, the store's and the config's.
````
