- [ ] **Step 1: The B3b design, as built**

Nearly every section changes, so the whole file:

Replace `docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md` with:

````markdown
# Phase B3b: one protocol node per role, and the kernel deleted

**Date:** 2026-10-27 · **Branch:** `feature/modularize` · **Status:** built, in the commits section 7 lists by subject
(a hash would go stale when the plan is re-executed); section 9 records what building it found.

Phase B of [modular-graph-design.md](modular-graph-design.md) moves the engine onto the graph in steps, each held bit
for bit to the B0 parity baseline ([modular-graph-phase-b0-design.md](modular-graph-phase-b0-design.md)). B3a
([modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md](modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md)) made the DSP kernel's input and output real
wires and ran the unchanged `DspKernel` as one TS script node, `rp.dsp.kernel`. B3b, the rest of "the kernel
dissolves", splits that node into one script node per role, folds `kernelProjection` into `buildGraph`, takes zod
out of the script-node bundle and deletes the kernel. The LSDj master-sync fix
([lsdj-master-sync-fix-design.md](lsdj-master-sync-fix-design.md)) landed between the two.

## 0. Where B3b sits

Before B3b the kernel node ran seven behaviours for the systems it was given, each a function over a per-system
context (`SystemCtx`) or the project's (`ProjectCtx`), in a fixed order every block: the project stages first (the
MIDI routing, which fanned the host's MIDI into a per-system inbox, then the Launchpad controller, which appended its
launches to its target's inbox), then each system's pipeline in slot order. Its structure (every system's roles, the
project stages) was its settings, which the stores published through `kernelProjection.ts`, and its outputs were one
port per system input plus one host MIDI out port whose messages carried a private 4-byte system-id prefix.

What the code said about splitting it:

- **No two roles on one system write the same system input.** mGB writes `serialIn`; LSDj writes `serialIn`,
  `buttons` and host MIDI out; a NES writes `midi` (`nes-n8-midi`) and, for a risa ROM, `bytes` (`risa-sync`); an
  SMS or GG writes `bytes`. So splitting needs no merge between protocols.
- **Tick state is per system, and no system has two ticking roles**, so a tick counter per node is the same.
- **One stream was merged**: the controller's launches joined its target system's routed MIDI, appended after the
  routed events at frame 0.
- **Host MIDI out was one port in emission order**: the controller's first, then the systems' in slot order, every
  message at frame 0.
- **The role registry is the app's model of roles**: each role's zod schema, `onConstruct` and menu stay on the
  control plane. Only each role's `dsp` behaviour was the kernel's.

## 1. Decisions taken

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| How is B3b cut? | **One design and one plan**, prototype first, then subagent-driven execution, as B3a. Every task stays bit-identical. |
| How does zod leave the audio side? | **A small zod-free settings schema** that `defineNode` takes (section 3). One bundle still serves both script runtimes; zod leaves the bundle entirely. |
| How is a protocol node written? | **Against the `Block` API**, as `rp.bench.pass` is: indexed loops over the input `Message` views, `send` on its own ports, state and tick counter on its instance, nothing allocated per block. The protocols' pure functions (the Arduinoboy and master-sync decoders, `routeBlockInto`, `risaLocate`, the SMS levels, `walkTicks`) and their unit tests stay as they are; only each role's glue around them is rewritten. |
| The capture mode as a Game Boy node setting? | **Not in B3b**: Phase C, with the other live knobs (`ConfigField` stays until then, as B2 decided). |
| Master-sync clocks at their byte's frame? | **Not in B3b**: it changes MIDI out, so it is its own change after B3b, with its own re-record. |
| One QuickJS context per script node? | **Not in B3b**: decided before user-written nodes (spec/07). |

## 2. The node set

Script nodes, one per role ([src/script/nodes/](../packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes)). Node ids follow the main
design's convention: `sys-<id>/<role-kind>` for a system's protocol node, `routing` and `controller` for the
project's.

| Type | Replaces | Inputs | Outputs | Settings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rp.midi.route` | `midi-routing` | `midiIn` | `sys-<id>`, one MIDI output per system, in slot order | `mode`; the system ids in slot order |
| `rp.mgb.midi` | `mgb` | `midi` | `serialIn` | none |
| `rp.n8.midi-to-fifo` | `nes-n8-midi` | `midiIn` (section 9) | `midi` | none |
| `rp.risa.sync` | `risa-sync` | none (the transport) | `bytes` | none |
| `rp.sms.sync` | `sms-sync` | none (the transport) | `bytes` | `machine` |
| `rp.lsdj.sync` | `lsdj-sync` | `midi`, `launches`, `serialOut` (a feedback wire, a Game Boy only) | `serialIn`, `buttons`, `midiOut` | `mode`, `tempoDivisor`, `autoStart` |
| `rp.controller.session` | `launchpad` | `controllerIn`, `controllerConnected` | `controllerOut`, `launches`, `midiOut` | its app, its target, the resolved system id, the parsed app config, the timing table, the anchor |

- Each protocol node's outputs are wired straight into its system node's inputs of the same name.
- `rp.lsdj.sync` reads its routed MIDI and then its launches, in that order, as the kernel's inbox held them. A
  frame merge would not be the same: the launches arrive at frame 0 after routed events at later frames.
- Every type is `reshapes: true`, so a config edit keeps the instance and its state, as the kernel's per-stage
  state survived a config change. A system removed and added again gets fresh instances, which the graph gives for
  free (the kernel pruned a dead id's state).
- `rp.lsdj.sync` keeps master sync's state in the sub-object the dispatcher drops outside the mode, as the role did.

## 3. Settings without zod, and the bundle

[`graph/settingsSchema.ts`](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema.ts), zod-free, is what `defineNode` takes:

- `s.object`, `s.enum(values, default)`, `s.int({ min, max, default })`, `s.bool(default)`, `s.number(default)`,
  `s.string(default)`, `s.array(item, default)` (the item carries a default of its own, section 9), and
  `s.json<T>(default)` for an opaque value the control plane has already checked (the controller's app config and
  its timing table).
- `safeParse(raw)` fills defaults and refuses bad input with today's one-line `field: why`; `toJSONSchema()` emits
  what zod's `toJSONSchema({ io: "input" })` emitted for the same shapes, which the shared golden descriptors pin
  byte for byte. Settings types are inferred (`Infer<typeof schema>`), as `z.infer` was.
- Every TS node type moves to it, the script test bundle's toy nodes included. Zod stays where the app already uses
  it: the role configs, the project files, the controller apps' configs.

The controller apps' registry paired each app's runtime with a zod schema, and the session parsed its app config
through it on the block thread. The publisher parses it on the control plane instead, where zod is loaded anyway
(`parseAppConfig` in [controller/registry.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/controller/registry.ts), section 9), and the
controller node imports only the apps' runtime, never the registry's schemas.

One bundle still serves both of an Engine's script runtimes, so the host's check that a node has the same
descriptor in both contexts is unchanged. It holds the protocol and controller nodes and nothing that registers
roles. A TS test bundles `script/bundle.ts` and fails if any zod module is in it, so the property holds on every
build. The bundle went from 660567 bytes in B3a, about 567 KB of it zod, to 78152 (section 9).

## 4. `buildGraph` and the stores

`buildGraph` places, in this order, every script node before the systems:

- the routing node, whenever the model has a MIDI routing mode (a project always has one; a `DirectGraph` or a lone
  `SystemsStore` routes none until a mode is set);
- the controller node when a controller is enabled, its default target ("0 is the first system") resolved to an id
  at the publish;
- each system's protocol nodes, in slot order;
- then the host I/O and the systems, as before.

`kernelProjection`'s special cases move in with it: the synthesized routing and controller nodes, and the forced
`rp.lsdj.sync` mode (`midiMap` or `off`) for the MI.MAP controller's target, written only into that node's settings,
so nothing of it reaches the `.rplg`, as before. The store's "roles the kernel runs" becomes "roles that have a
protocol node", one table ([graph/protocolNodes.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/protocolNodes.ts), section 9).

A profile build's `apu-render` span begins where the last script node's `process` ended, which is right only while
every script node runs before the systems. The planner keeps document order among nodes ready at once
([Planner.cpp](../packages/native/src/graph/Planner.cpp) `order()`), so the span needed no change.

## 5. Host I/O, capacities, and what must match

**Host MIDI out by wiring.** `rp.host.midi-out` becomes a native node set by `{ systems: [id, ...] }`, one input per
entry, `in1` to `inN` (as `rp.core.merge` takes `{"inputs": N}`); an empty list is a node with no inputs. Each block
it appends each input's messages, input by input in order, under that input's system id. `buildGraph` orders the
inputs as the kernel emitted: the controller's `midiOut` first (under its resolved target), then each
`rp.lsdj.sync` in slot order. The 4-byte system prefix goes with the kernel; every host MIDI out message stays at
frame 0, as before. `rp.host.controller-out` is unchanged (one producer).

**Capacities**, port for port as the kernel's ([nodes/ports.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/ports.ts)):
`serialIn` and `midi` 4096 messages / 72 KiB, `bytes` 256 / 1 KiB, `buttons` 64 / 128 bytes, `midiOut` 1024 / 8 KiB,
`controllerOut` 256 / 4 KiB. A routing output takes `rp.host.midi-in`'s capacity (2048 messages / 64 KiB), since
under send-to-all it carries everything the input passed; `launches` is small (64 messages / 256 bytes). Drops stay
counted per port.

**What must match the kernel exactly**, each checked by the equivalence test (section 6):

1. Within a node, each port's emission order is what the kernel emitted for that system and sink, so the
   out-of-order senders (Arduinoboy's START after a row byte, MI.MAP's clocks after its rows) get the same clamp-up
   from the frame-ordered queue.
2. Host MIDI out's order across nodes.
3. Launches after routed events.
4. Tick counters and state as the per-system ones were, across a config edit, a removal, and a re-add.
5. The MIDI-channel-to-instance rewritten copy.
6. The controller's default target.

How messages are grouped is free where no core can see it: `rp.mgb.midi` sends each MIDI message's bytes as one
`serialIn` message at its frame where the kernel coalesced all same-frame bytes; a system node applies a message's
bytes in order, and the digests hash `serialIn` byte by byte. Every other port is hashed message by message, so those
nodes send the kernel's messages as they were.

**A throw** keeps the node's output up to the throw, counted, and its next block runs again: the kernel's rule, per
node. One difference: a throw in one system's node no longer drops later systems' output for that block. No parity
case throws.

## 6. Testing

- **Equivalence.** The C++ kernel-node rig's cases (every LSDj mode, risa and smsggdj sync, NES MIDI, a controller
  session whose launches interleave with MI.OUT, structure changes with state surviving) are rebuilt on the per-role
  graph, their document generated as `buildGraph` places it, and must hold their recorded digests unchanged (recorded
  while the old kernel stage ran beside the kernel node). The rig's thread-sanitizer case (the control side
  restructuring while the audio thread runs) moves over too. Built:
  [ProtocolNodes.test.cpp](../packages/native/test/engine-graph/ProtocolNodes.test.cpp).
- **Node-level tests.** The role tests that drive `DspKernel` (roles, LSDj modes, routing, risa, sms, the controller,
  ticks, the kernel-level Arduinoboy and master-sync cases) port to node-level tests over a `Block` stand-in, as
  `kernel-node.test.ts` already drove one; the pure-function tests stay; `project-ctx`'s kernel-specific cases go
  with the kernel. Built: `test/script/nodes/`, one file per type.
- **`buildGraph`.** The explicit wiring tables are updated and `kernelProjection`'s tests move here (the controller's
  sync override, the synthesized nodes); the goldens are re-recorded by a one-off script, and the native golden
  runner still plans and runs every one with no fault, throw or drop.
- **The bundle.** The no-zod test; the bench re-pointed at the per-role node set at 1, 64 and 512 frames; the profile
  benches (`dsp-bench`, `nes-bench`) and spec/08's figures.
- **Parity**, strict at every task, nothing re-recorded.
- **Acceptance**, B3a's full matrix: strict parity with the fixtures and `RP_FAIL_ON_SKIP=1`, and the CI view (an
  unfiltered `test:native` with the fixture directories absent, since a filtered run does not judge the skip
  baseline); `test:native`, `pnpm test`, plugin, ui and node suites; the thread and address sanitizers (with the
  fixtures, so `dsp-threaded` runs); the Reaper suite; `sdl:pipewire`; BlipToaster, NESVJ and `cli-ts`.

## 7. How it lands

Every commit bit-identical. As built, each step's commit named by its subject:

1. The zod-free settings schema; `defineNode` and the toy nodes on it ("feat(graph): a zod-free settings schema that
   defineNode takes beside zod's, and the toy nodes on it").
2. The seven node types and their node-level tests, in the bundle beside the kernel node, not yet placed ("feat(dsp):
   one script node per role - routing, mGB, N8, risa, smsggdj, LSDj and the controller session - beside the kernel,
   not yet placed").
3. `rp.host.midi-out`'s `systems` form, beside its prefixed form ("feat(engine): rp.host.midi-out takes each input's
   system from its settings, beside its prefixed form"). It moved ahead of the equivalence rig, which needs it
   (section 9).
4. The equivalence rig over the per-role graph, holding the recorded digests ("test(engine): the kernel node's
   recorded digests, held by the per-role graph as by the kernel").
5. The flip: `buildGraph` places the per-role graph, `kernelProjection` folded in; the stores publish it; the goldens
   re-recorded ("feat(graph): the kernel dissolved into the graph - buildGraph places one protocol node per role, the
   routing and the controller, kernelProjection folded in").
6. The deletion: the kernel node, `DspKernel`, the roles' `dsp` behaviours and the role type's `dsp` field, the
   prefixed host MIDI out, the kernel-based tests; the bundle's last zod goes with them, and the no-zod test passes
   ("refactor(dsp): delete the DSP kernel - DspKernel, the kernel node and the roles' behaviours; the script-node
   bundle holds no zod"). `kernelProjection` had already gone in the flip.
7. The bench and the profiles ("test(engine): the bench and the profiles on the per-role nodes - each script node's
   span names its type").
8. Docs: this design's status and section 9, the main design and B3a's, every spec doc that described the kernel
   (spec/04 renamed to [04-roles-protocol-nodes.md](../spec/04-roles-protocol-nodes.md)), AGENTS.md, and the code
   comments that still spoke of the kernel as present ("docs: B3b built - the protocol nodes, the zod-free bundle and
   the kernel's deletion, and what building it found").
9. Acceptance (section 6).

## 8. Left for later

- The capture mode as a Game Boy node setting, which makes a mode switch atomic (Phase C).
- Master-sync clocks at their byte's frame (its own change after B3b). It would be the first producer of host MIDI
  past frame 0, and `rp.host.midi-out` appends input by input, so the host's list would then need a merge by frame
  across its inputs, or the hosts a sort before they write it out.
- One QuickJS context per script node (before user-written nodes).
- The MI.OUT and master-sync decoders' emitted arrays: about 3 JS allocations for every host MIDI message they
  decode, the one per-block JS allocation left on a production path (section 9). It is the decoders' own change, in
  `lsdjArduinoboy.ts`'s pure functions, not the node's.
- `defineNode` itself keeps to ES2015's library (`Set`, `Object.entries`, `includes`), so the bundle is zod-free but
  not yet MicroQuickJS-ready; `settingsSchema.ts` already keeps to ES5's.

## 9. Found while building

- **The role-to-node mapping is a table, not a `RoleType` field.** Section 4 left open where "roles that have a
  protocol node" is decided, and a `node` field on `RoleType` was the obvious place. It is
  [graph/protocolNodes.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/protocolNodes.ts) instead, pure, zod-free and registry-free:
  each role kind with a node, the node type it is placed as, and how `buildGraph` wires that type (the input its routed
  MIDI arrives on, the system inputs it writes, whether it takes launches, serial out or sends host MIDI). The node
  types are code in the bundle every Engine embeds, so which role kinds have one is a fact of that bundle, not of
  whichever registry a store was handed; and three publishers need it, two of which hold no registry at all (a
  `DirectGraph`, and a `SystemsStore` built without one, as the tests build them). A field on `RoleType` would need
  this table as its fallback anyway, which makes two sources that can disagree about a role. Two tests hold it: the
  registry test that it names a node for exactly the roles `registerDspRoles` registers, and `build-graph.test.ts`
  that its type ids are the node modules' own (importing the modules would pull every protocol into whatever imports
  `buildGraph`).
- **Host MIDI out by wiring came before the equivalence rig.** Section 7 had the rig third and `rp.host.midi-out`'s
  `systems` form fourth. The rig builds the per-role document, and without the systems form that document has no way
  to say whose host MIDI is whose: the prefixed form needs a 4-byte prefix that no protocol node writes. So the systems
  form landed first, beside the prefixed form, and the rig wired it. As built it takes inputs `in1` to `inN`, 1-based
  as `rp.core.merge`'s, at most 128 (`kMidiOutMaxSystems`, so a commit copies the ids into a fixed array without
  allocating); any 32-bit id, 0 and 4294967295 included, and one id may repeat. Its prepare is stateless: a settings
  change that keeps the inputs is a swap, one that moves them a rebuild.
- **An empty `systems` list means no inputs.** The flip placed `{"systems": []}` when nothing sends host MIDI, which
  until the deletion was the prefixed form, unwired. With the prefixed form gone, an empty list is a node with no
  inputs that sends nothing, and `buildGraph` still places it, so a document has its host outputs whatever its roles;
  no golden document changed. The prefix was the one way `rp.host.midi-out` dropped a message (one too short to carry
  it), so the engine's count of those went with it: `Engine::droppedMessages` is now the plan's queues alone. The host
  service keeps its interface id, `rp.engine.host-io/1`.
- **Port names.** The N8 node's input is `midiIn`, where section 2 said `midi`: its output is named for the system
  input it feeds, `midi`, as every protocol node's is, and a port id names one port. `buildGraph` reads each type's
  MIDI input from the table. The routing node's outputs are `sys-<id>`, and its layout refuses two systems under one
  id, which the kernel's zod settings refused with a refinement the zod-free schema has no way to say.
- **The controller's app config is parsed by the publisher, not by `buildGraph`.** Section 3 had `buildGraph` parse
  it; `buildGraph` stays pure and registry-free instead, and the publisher parses it: `ProjectStore.controllerModel`
  for a project, `DirectGraph.setController` for the rest, each through `parseAppConfig(id, raw)` in
  [controller/registry.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/controller/registry.ts), which gives an id no app has an empty
  config (its node then runs nothing). The apps' runtime moved to a zod-free
  [controller/apps/index.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/controller/apps/index.ts), which the node imports; the registry
  pairs each runtime with its menu label and its zod schema, and refuses, when it registers, an app with no schema.
  The rest of what `kernelProjection` did lives in [graph/controller.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/controller.ts):
  the target resolution, the MI.MAP override and the node's settings. The controller node also imports the playback
  predictor's leaf module rather than the `lsdj/playback` barrel, which would have pulled the WRAM reader and the sav
  codec into the bundle.
- **The `midi-routing` and `launchpad` roles are gone, and with them `RoleType`'s `dsp` and `scope` and
  `isSystemStage`.** Only the kernel read them as roles: the MIDI routing and the controller are project settings, which
  `kernelProjection` synthesized into those roles and `buildGraph` now places as nodes, so nothing persisted names
  them. [dspRoles.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/dspRoles.ts) keeps the five roles that have a protocol node, each its
  kind, its zod config schema and, for LSDj, the empty-sav seed hook; `registerDspRoles` keeps its name, since what it
  registers are still the roles whose work is the audio thread's.
- **`DirectGraph`'s `setProjectStages` became `setMidiRouting` and `setController`.** The flip mapped it onto the new
  model; the deletion removed it, since it spelled the routing and the controller as the two roles that went, and its
  19 calling files moved. A `DirectGraph`'s controller now gets the target resolution and the MI.MAP override a
  project's does, since `buildGraph` applies both to any model.
- **The spans are named by node type.** The kernel traced each role's stage as a span inside its one node's
  `process` span, through span globals bound into the audio context. Each role is a node now, so the script host labels
  each script node's `process` span by its type: the bundle's types take labels from `DSP_SPAN_TYPE_BASE` (16) up, in
  registration order, each named by its id. By type rather than node id, since the kernel's role spans were per kind
  too, a type's label is fixed when the bundle loads (one per id would come and go with every document), and a node's
  `create` is never told its id; two systems' nodes of one type show as two spans a block, in plan order. `dsp-kernel`
  became `script-node` (`DSP_SPAN_SCRIPT_NODE`, label 0), now only the fallback for a type past the 1024-label bound.
  The span globals (`spanBegin`, `spanEnd`, `traceName`, `traceArmed`) and the floor and fence that kept JS's spans
  inside the host's went: the kernel's roles were their only user. The profile build's `[profile]` cases went from five
  to four ([spec/08](../spec/08-profiling.md)).
- **The profile benches proved themselves live by allocating.** `dsp-bench` and `nes-bench` checked that their
  counters worked by an allocation count above zero, which the allocation-free nodes broke: `dsp-bench` failed under
  the profile host from the deletion until the bench commit (nothing in the default suites runs it), which checks the
  audio runtime's peak heap instead.
- **The settings schema, as built.** Each `s` builder parses and writes its JSON Schema as its zod twin does, held by
  `test/graph/settings-schema.test.ts` to zod's own output over 34 values, refusals in zod's own English words, and an
  object drops a key it does not name, as `z.object` does. An array's item needs a default of its own, though parse
  never uses it, since zod writes an item's `.default` into the schema; and `s.json` takes its type as an explicit
  parameter, since a default such as `{}` says nothing about it. `defineNode` takes any schema with `safeParse` and
  `toJSONSchema`, so a zod schema still serves on the control plane (`define-node.test.ts` keeps one zod case on
  purpose). The script test bundle's toy nodes moved too, which took that bundle from 588942 bytes to 21537.
- **The bundle: 78152 bytes, 34 modules** (49908 bytes of bytecode), against 660567 before B3b (687646 at the flip,
  the seven node types beside the kernel). Getting zod out took two zod-free splits besides the controller apps':
  the LSDj link constants and `midiMapRow` into `lsdjSyncBytes.ts`, out of `dspRoles.ts` and its schemas, and
  `walkTicks` into `ticks.ts`, out of the kernel's module. `test/script/bundle-no-zod.test.ts` builds the bundle with
  the build's own options (`tools/build-session.js` exports them) and fails on any zod module in esbuild's metafile,
  and on the role and config modules (`configSchema`, `systemRoles`, `dspRoles`, `coreRoles`, `projectConfig`). The
  bundle's load leaves no cycles in the audio runtime, where B3a's left about 144 KiB for the first quiescent reclaim
  to collect: the `[script][gc]` case that holds that collection now loads a chunk of its own that leaves one.
- **What the equivalence rig showed.** Every recorded digest held on the per-role graph, run beside the kernel node's
  graph from the rig's commit to the flip, and alone since. One case reads a per-node difference, the throw (section
  5): in the block where the second system's LSDj node throws, the third system's mGB node still forwards its MIDI,
  which the case checks, and that block's digest takes the third system as the kernel left it, with nothing. One case
  is new, recorded from the kernel node when the rig was built: a controller with its default target launching
  immediately, behind routed MIDI into an MI.MAP cart, then out of the host in blocks where two Game Boys send host
  MIDI too. Section 5's items 2, 3 and 6 were orders no earlier case sent a message through (the controller case
  staged no host MIDI, and its one launch to the host was cued past its last block), so without it the rig could not
  have caught a change in them. Before the rig, a temporary TS cross-check drove `DspKernel` and each node through the
  same blocks and compared every port; it caught 29 of 30 deliberate mutations of the nodes and went with the kernel.
  The thread sanitizer ran the rig's cases clean, and the restructuring one five times more.
- **The flip moved no audio.** The goldens were re-recorded by a one-off script, 840 cases and 238 documents, and the
  audio part of every document is as it was. Strict parity held bit for bit at every commit, nothing re-recorded.
- **Behaviour that differs from the kernel**, none of which a parity case sees:
  - A node's state is keyed by its role's kind (`sys-<id>/<kind>`), where the kernel keyed a stage's by its system and
    its place in the pipeline. So a role removed and added again on a surviving system starts afresh, and a role no
    longer inherits a neighbour's state when a role ahead of it is added or removed.
  - The controller's default target follows a change of first system: the resolved id is in the node's settings and
    in what rebuilds its session, where the kernel's session kept the id it resolved when it was built.
  - The controller rebuilds its session when its parsed app config changes, where the kernel compared the raw config,
    so an edit the app's schema reads as no change keeps the session.
  - Launches go only into a "system" target's `rp.lsdj.sync`; the kernel appended them to the target's inbox, which an
    mGB or a NES stage would have forwarded to the core.
  - `onSettings` runs only on a real change; the kernel re-applied the song table on every push, which nothing could
    observe.
  - A pipeline's configs must be what the store parsed: a node's settings fill their defaults (an `lsdj-sync` with no
    mode is `midiSync`), where the kernel's roles read a missing field as nothing. The stores hand parsed configs; a
    `DirectGraph` caller passes its own as given.
  - A throw stops only the node it is in (section 5).
  - The routing always runs before the controller; the kernel ran its project stages in the order given, which the
    stores always gave as routing first.
  - Where a system has no protocol node for an input, or no controller is enabled, the input or the host I/O node is
    left unwired, where the kernel node's outputs were wired and sent nothing.
- **The bench** ([ScriptBench.test.cpp](../packages/native/test/engine-graph/ScriptBench.test.cpp), hidden:
  `build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test "[bench]"`; Release, 44.1 kHz, a Ryzen 9 9950X, medians of 7 runs, three runs
  as ranges). A script node's call is as B3a measured it: 0.084 to 0.092 us a node with nothing to pass and 0.172 to
  0.199 us with one message in and out, flat in node count and block size, with no JS or native allocation; 64 nodes
  take 5.74 to 5.88 us, or 11.8 to 12.1 us with a message each. The protocol nodes are timed in their plan, the routing
  and a node a system, wired as `buildGraph` wires them, over B3a's structure (mGB, an LSDj and a NES on
  `nes-n8-midi`, send-to-all, playing at 120 bpm, a host message every 441 frames, the LSDj's serial out a byte every 8
  frames), against the same plan with no script nodes; no core runs:

  | Block | LSDj in MIDI sync | LSDj in MI.OUT, decoding | The plan alone | JS allocations a block (MIDI sync / MI.OUT) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 frame | 0.933 to 0.954 us | 0.835 to 0.853 us | 0.030 to 0.031 us | 0 / 0.23 |
  | 64 frames | 2.214 to 2.232 us | 3.883 to 3.899 us | 0.040 to 0.043 us | 0 / 15 |
  | 512 frames | 10.78 to 11.36 us | 23.24 to 23.87 us | 0.099 to 0.101 us | 0 / 120 |

  In MIDI sync the nodes allocate nothing, JS or native. The MI.OUT row feeds the LSDj a framed command every 8
  frames (clocks, a note on and off, a CC: five host MIDI messages in every 8 bytes) and checks that the host gets
  every one; its allocations are about 3 for each decoded message, the decoder's emitted arrays (section 8). Against B3a's last kernel-node figures (2.68 to
  2.74, 7.69 to 7.92 and 39.5 to 40.7 us, with 25, 81 and 431 JS allocations a block, measured on another tree and
  day), the per-role nodes in MIDI sync are about 2.9, 3.5 and 3.6 times faster. Part of that is B3a section 9's advice
  taken: only an LSDj's serial out is wired, into its own node, where the B3a bench also fed the kernel mGB's idle
  bytes. The rest is the kernel node's per-block `BlockInput` copy, which B3a's bench found to be its per-message
  cost, gone.
- **The profile benches** (`tools/run-profile.sh stats`, Profile A): `dsp-bench` makes 0 allocations a block (B3a:
  33.81), 0 in its worst block (62), with a peak heap of 307096 bytes, at 15.8 times real time; `nes-bench` 0 (20.14) and
  0 (44), peak 305064 bytes, at 10.3 times real time. The end-of-window collection frees nothing in either. A trace of
  `dsp-bench` (`tools/run-profile.sh trace`) has `rp.midi.route` at 1.37 us a block and `rp.mgb.midi` at 0.83, each
  holding a `js-call` of about 0.95 and its `marshal` spans of about 0.11, against 1428 us of `apu-render` and 2.0 of
  `state-publish`; `nes-bench`'s has `rp.midi.route` at 1.09 us and `rp.n8.midi-to-fifo` at 0.53, against 2151 of
  `apu-render` and 3.7 of `state-publish` ([spec/08](../spec/08-profiling.md)).
````

Create `spec/04-roles-protocol-nodes.md`:

````markdown
# 04 - Roles & the protocol nodes

Roles are how RetroPlug attaches *meaning* to a system without teaching the C++ cores anything.
A role is a `{ kind, config }` pair keyed by a string; the core treats `config` as an opaque
per-kind blob. Everything specific to a system (a backend's emulator knobs, or an optional
feature like LSDj sync or mGB passthrough) is a role, so the cores stay free of backend/LSDj/mGB
knowledge. Cores are built **bare** (`setSniffDefaultRoles(false)`); every feature behaviour lives in
TypeScript, and a role whose work is the audio thread's runs as a **protocol node**: a TS script node
of its own in the engine's graph, which `buildGraph` places for each system that has the role.

This is the sharpest expression of the thesis (*"native owns bytes and cores; TypeScript owns
meaning"*): the same node code runs over a `Block` stand-in in the unit tests and on the audio thread
in the script host, and native carries the bundle and each node's settings without interpreting
either. Until B3b ([modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md](../docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md)) one
TS DSP kernel ran every role inside one script node; each role is its own node now, and the kernel is
gone.

This doc covers the role model and the protocol nodes end to end. For the runtime plumbing the nodes
ride on (the command ring, the QuickJS runtimes, the audio-thread ownership model), see
[01-architecture.md](01-architecture.md); this doc references those concepts rather than
re-explaining them. For the C++ script host the nodes run in, see [02-native-host.md](02-native-host.md).

## The two role kinds

| | **system-role** | **feature-role** |
|---|---|---|
| Carries | a backend's live emulator knobs | a feature's settings (a sync mode, an asset override) |
| Attached by | backend/core kind | ROM identity (a `RomProvider`) |
| `category` | `"system"` | `"feature"` |
| Examples today | `sameboy`, `mesen` | `mgb`, `lsdj-sync`, `risa-sync`, `lsdj-assets` |
| Config reaches the live core? | **yes**: the only role config that crosses, via `applyRoleConfig` | **no**: its config never gets a C++ struct |
| Where behaviour lives | inside the core (native applies the fields) | its protocol node, when it has one; otherwise the control plane (an asset override is folded into the ROM there) |

The dividing line is load-bearing: **only a system-role's config crosses the RPC boundary into the
live emulator**. A feature-role's config is pure TS: for a role with a protocol node it travels only as
that node's settings in the graph document the project publishes (below).

## The role model

Five pieces make up the generic model, in [systemRoles.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/systemRoles.ts).
It ports the shape of the native `RoleConfig` tagged union into a runtime registry, minus the
hardcoded if/else chains.

### `RoleInstance`: what serializes

```ts
interface RoleInstance { kind: string; config: Record<string, unknown>; }
```

A system carries an ordered `RoleInstance[]`. This is the persisted form (part of `SystemEntry`);
config is an opaque per-kind blob whose schema the role owns.

### `RoleType`: a registry entry

Contributed by the built-ins (or, eventually, an extension). Fields
([systemRoles.ts:52](../packages/retroplug/src/systemRoles.ts#L52)):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | the string key (for a system-role, `kind` IS the core, e.g. `"sameboy"`) |
| `category` | `"system"` or `"feature"` |
| `schema` | a zod schema whose `.parse` fills defaults + clamps a partial/invalid config into a full one; `.parse({})` yields the default config |
| `onConstruct?` | a load-time hook that transforms the resolved `ConstructSpec` just before the core is built (ADDITIVE by contract: seed only what's otherwise absent) |
| `ui?` | **deferred**: a UI-thread behaviour + settings render descriptor (see [Not yet built](#not-yet-built--deferred)) |

A role type says nothing about the audio thread. Which role kinds have a protocol node, and which node
each is placed as, is one table beside `buildGraph` ([Store → graph](#store--graph)), not a field here:
the node types are code in the bundle every Engine embeds, so that is a fact of the bundle, and two of
the three publishers that need it hold no registry.

### `RoleRegistry`: the kind-keyed store

[`RoleRegistry`](../packages/retroplug/src/systemRoles.ts#L94) holds a `Map<kind, RoleType>`
plus a list of `RomProvider`s:

| Method | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `registerRole(t)` / `registerRomProvider(fn)` | populate the registry |
| `roleType(kind)` | look up a `RoleType` |
| `systemRoleFor(core)` | the `"system"` role whose kind === the core, or none |
| `defaultRoles(core, platform, header, embeddedRom)` | the default `RoleInstance[]` for a fresh system: the core's config role (if any) followed by every provider's feature-role suggestions, each `schema.parse`d |

### `RomProvider` + `RomContext`: feature-role attachment

A `RomProvider` inspects a freshly-classified ROM and returns the feature roles to attach. It is the
TS twin of the C++ `RomSniffer`'s default-role step:

```ts
type RomProvider = (rom: RomContext) => RoleInstance[];
// RomContext = { platform, core, header (cartridge title @ 0x134), embeddedRom }
```

The built-ins ([romProviders.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/romProviders.ts)) match on ROM
identity:

| Provider | Match | Attaches |
|---|---|---|
| mGB | embedded marker `"mgb"`, or cartridge title starting `MGB` | `mgb` |
| LSDj | cartridge title starting `LSDJ` (stock or arduinoboy build) | `lsdj-sync` (`midiSync`) and `lsdj-assets` |
| NES | every NES ROM | `nes-n8-midi` |
| smsggdj | the SMSGGDJ build marker, on a Master System or Game Gear | `sms-sync` (`machine` the platform) |
| risa | its iNES 2.0 header fingerprint (MMC5 + a 64 KB battery) | `risa` and `risa-assets`, and `risa-sync` for a build with the `RISA-SYNC` marker |
| BlipToaster | the `bliptoaster` marker in the ROM head | `bliptoaster` and `bliptoaster-assets` |

The embedded-ROM **marker** is the only signal for a baked-in synth, whose bytes never reach TS, so
its header is empty and the provider matches on the marker instead. ROM providers are registered into
the **control-plane** registry only; the script-node bundle never sees a role, a schema or a provider.

### `ConstructCaps` + `onConstruct` hooks

`onConstruct` runs at construct time for each role actually attached to a system (so it is inherently
ROM-gated), transforming the resolved `ConstructSpec`. It sees only a narrow `ConstructCaps` slice
(`savFromJson`, `fileExists`, `readFile`, `pngDecode`), which the full `Backend` satisfies structurally,
so the store passes itself.

LSDj's empty-sav seed ([dspRoles.ts:16](../packages/retroplug/src/dspRoles.ts#L16)) is the plainest: a
fresh LSDj cart with no save data runs a 12-15 s cartridge self-test on boot. When nothing else will seed
the battery (no savestate, no SRAM blob, no on-disk `.sav` for native to load) the hook hands it a valid
empty sav via `savFromJson("{}")` so LSDj boots straight to the song screen. It is additive: the spec is
returned untouched when real save data is present. The asset roles' hooks fold their overrides into the
ROM in memory the same way.

### Where derivation happens in the store

[SystemsStore](../packages/retroplug/src/systemsStore.ts) drives the registry:
`defaultRoles(...)` reads a `ROLE_HEADER_LEN = 0x150` header prefix and calls
`registry.defaultRoles(...)`
([systemsStore.ts:749](../packages/retroplug/src/systemsStore.ts#L749)); `applyConstructHooks`
folds each attached role's `onConstruct` over the spec before the build call
([systemsStore.ts:853](../packages/retroplug/src/systemsStore.ts#L853)). See
[03-ts-layer.md](03-ts-layer.md) for the surrounding store idioms.

## The built-in roles

The control-plane registry ([appHost.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/appHost.ts) `buildAppRegistry`)
takes `registerCoreRoles`, `registerDspRoles`, the asset and marker roles (`lsdj-assets`, `risa`,
`risa-assets`, `bliptoaster`, `bliptoaster-assets`) and `registerRomProviders`.

**System roles** ([coreRoles.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/coreRoles.ts)), keyed by core
value, ranges mirroring the native enums:

| Role | Config (zod, defaults) |
|---|---|
| `sameboy` | `model` 0-13 (CgbC=9), `highpass` 0-2, `linkGroupId` 0-255, `fastBoot` bool (true), plus the display group (`colorCorrection`, `dmgPalette`, `lightTemperature`) |
| `mesen` | one role for every Mesen platform, so the knobs are per-platform and the menu gates each group. NES: `region`, `removeSpriteLimit`, `apuLatencyMs`, the cartridge-accuracy pair (`s5bNoise` / `mmc5PhaseReset`, both defaulting to `"n8"`), `expansionVolume` (the cartridge sound chip's level, percent of unity: the same value the UI rescales into a connected N8's `master_vol`), `channelExportMode`, `sdRoot`. SMS/GG: `enableFm` |

Not every system-role field is live. `region`, `channelExportMode` and `sdRoot` are read when the core
is **constructed**, so an edit takes effect only after a rebuild: `setRoleConfig(id, …)` then
`reset(id)`, which re-sends the stored role config as the construct `settings` blob and hands back a
new id. `sdRoot` is the host directory the emulated EverDrive N8 SD card maps to (`"/"` on the card),
for a NES ROM that pulls its data off the cartridge; empty means a per-process scratch directory, not
the working directory. Reading back what such a ROM sends is `drainCoreBytes` ([09](09-cli-debugging.md)).
A ROM can also skip the CPU entirely: `CMD_F_FRD_MEM` has the emulated MCU read the open file straight
into cartridge memory over the PI bus, which `MesenNesSystem` backs for the CHR-RAM window
(PI `0xC00000`) only. That transfer's duration is modelled from the rate measured on real hardware,
so the ROM's wait loop spins about as long here as it does on a console.

`fifo` (plus the `fifoDepth` / `fifoBytesPerSecond` overrides) says how faithfully that FIFO behaves
like the cartridge's. It defaults to `"instant"` (unbounded and delivered immediately, which is what
every existing test assumes), and `"hardware"` opts in to 2048 bytes deep, dropping when full, fed at
the wire's ~150 KB/s. Both of those absences hide a bug class rather than being bugs: a ROM that
cannot lose a byte never has its recovery path exercised, and one handed a whole chunk atomically is
never starved mid-structure. `getCoreTransportStats` reports both queue depths and the cumulative
drop count ([09](09-cli-debugging.md)).

**Roles with a protocol node** ([dspRoles.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/dspRoles.ts)): each registers its
kind, its zod config schema (the shape the stores parse, persist and hand the node as its settings) and,
for LSDj, the seed hook. What each does on the audio thread is its node's
([The protocol nodes](#the-protocol-nodes)):

| Role | Node | Config |
|---|---|---|
| `mgb` | `rp.mgb.midi` | none |
| `nes-n8-midi` | `rp.n8.midi-to-fifo` | none |
| `risa-sync` | `rp.risa.sync` | none |
| `sms-sync` | `rp.sms.sync` | `machine`: `"sms"` or `"gg"` |
| `lsdj-sync` | `rp.lsdj.sync` | `mode` (an `LsdjSyncMode`, default `midiSync`), `tempoDivisor` 1-8, `autoStart` |

The MIDI routing and the control-surface controller are **project settings**, not roles
([05-data-persistence.md](05-data-persistence.md)): `buildGraph` places a node for each from the
project's settings, as it places a protocol node for a role.

## Which config reaches the live core

Two channels cross the RPC boundary to a running emulator, and no feature-role config uses either:

| Change | RPC | Reaches |
|---|---|---|
| the two universal settings (`gainDb`, `reloadOnRomChange`) | `applySystemSetting` | the live core (see [03-ts-layer.md](03-ts-layer.md)) |
| a **system-role** config edit | `applyRoleConfig(id, kind, config)` | the live core (`sameboy` + `mesen`), minus the construct-time fields noted above |
| a **feature-role** config edit | *(none to the core)* | only its protocol node, as its settings in the next document the project publishes |

[`SystemsStore.setRoleConfig`](../packages/retroplug/src/systemsStore.ts#L525) merges the
partial, re-parses through the role schema, and calls `backend.applyRoleConfig` **only when the role's
`category === "system"`**. On the native side
[`EngineRpcService::applyRoleConfig`](../packages/native/src/host/rpc/EngineRpcService.cpp#L165)
accepts `kind == "sameboy"` and `"mesen"`, decodes the whole role config, and pushes each field as a
guarded config field (an unchanged field is a no-op, so moving `highpass` never triggers a spurious
model restart).

A **feature**-role config edit takes a different path: `setRoleConfig` updates TS state and, for a
role that has a protocol node, publishes the graph (`setOnGraphChange` → `ProjectStore.publishGraph`),
in which that node's settings are the role's parsed config; the planner hands the node its new settings
at the plan swap (`onSettings`), keeping the instance and its state, since every protocol node reshapes.
An edit to a role with no node (an asset override) changes no document. Then `markDirty` fires the
systems `onChange` → the project's `onSystemsChange`
([projectStore.ts:215](../packages/retroplug/src/projectStore.ts#L215)) for the structure's
observers. The core is never told, with one exception: an `lsdj-sync` mode change sets the Game Boy's
serial-out capture (`setSerialOutCapture`), which the two MIDI-out modes decode: `drive` for MI.OUT, where
the core plays the Arduinoboy that clocks LSDj, and `listen` for master sync, where LSDj clocks itself.

## The protocol nodes

Seven TS node types ([src/script/nodes/](../packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes)), each a `defineNode`
in the script-node bundle ([script/bundle.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/script/bundle.ts)): the MIDI
routing, a protocol node for each role that has one, and the control-surface session. Each is its
protocol's glue around pure functions that stay where they were (the Arduinoboy and master-sync
decoders in `lsdjArduinoboy.ts`, `routeTarget` in `midiRouting.ts`, `risaLocate` / `risaArmPacket` in
`risaSync.ts`, `syncLevelsFor` in `smsSync.ts`, `walkTicks` in `ticks.ts`, the LSDj keyboard map and
link bytes), and each is held to the kernel it replaced by the recorded digests of
[ProtocolNodes.test.cpp](../packages/native/test/engine-graph/ProtocolNodes.test.cpp).

| Type | Placed for | Inputs | Outputs | Settings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rp.midi.route` | the project (`routing`) | `midiIn` | `sys-<id>` for each system, in slot order | `mode` (a `MidiRouting`, default `sendToAll`), `systems` (the ids in slot order) |
| `rp.mgb.midi` | `mgb` | `midi` | `serialIn` | none |
| `rp.n8.midi-to-fifo` | `nes-n8-midi` | `midiIn` | `midi` | none |
| `rp.risa.sync` | `risa-sync` | none (the transport) | `bytes` | none |
| `rp.sms.sync` | `sms-sync` | none (the transport) | `bytes` | `machine` |
| `rp.lsdj.sync` | `lsdj-sync` | `midi`, `launches`, `serialOut` | `serialIn`, `buttons`, `midiOut` | `mode`, `tempoDivisor`, `autoStart` |
| `rp.controller.session` | the project's controller (`controller`) | `controllerIn` (events), `controllerConnected` (control) | `controllerOut`, `launches`, `midiOut` | `app`, `target`, `systemId` (resolved: 0 is none), `appConfig` (parsed), `songRowTicks`, `anchorRows`, `anchorSeq` |

**How they are written.** Against the `Block` API, as the bench's pass-through is: indexed loops over
the input `Message` views, `send` on the node's own ports, state and the tick counter on the instance
(made in `create`), nothing allocated per block. Measured, the routing, mGB, N8 and LSDj MIDI-sync nodes
allocate nothing in a warm block, JS or native ([08-profiling.md](08-profiling.md)); what still allocates is
work that makes something: risa's arm packet on a start or a seek, the controller session's surface diff and
launches, and the LSDj node's two MIDI-out decoders' emitted messages. Every type declares `reshapes`, so a
settings change keeps the instance and its state, even one that changes its ports (the routing node's
outputs follow the systems); a system removed and added again gets fresh nodes.

**What each does per block:**

- **`rp.midi.route`** fans the host's MIDI out to the systems: each message goes, at its own frame and
  in the order it came, to every system (`sendToAll`, and always for a SysEx or a system message), or to
  one by its channel's position among them (`fourChannelsPerInstance`: channel / 4, `oneChannelPerInstance`
  and `midiChannelToInstance`: the channel, each modulo the system count), by `routeTarget`'s arithmetic.
  `midiChannelToInstance` hands its target a copy with the channel rewritten to 0, from a buffer made once.
  System order is authoritative: the positional modes route by a system's index in `systems`. Its layout
  refuses two systems under one id.
- **`rp.mgb.midi`** sends each routed message's bytes as one `serialIn` message at its frame, which is all
  mGB listens for (the system node applies a message's bytes in order at its frame).
- **`rp.n8.midi-to-fifo`** sends each routed message whole to the NES core's `midi` input, which feeds the
  always-attached N8 FIFO. Its input is `midiIn` because its output is named for the system input it
  feeds, as every protocol node's is.
- **`rp.risa.sync`** drives risa's N8-FIFO host-sync receive path from the transport alone: on a rise, or a
  ppq discontinuity while playing (a seek or a loop), a 5-byte arm+locate computed from the block-start
  ppq, flushing the FIFO (`RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH`), then START; on a fall, STOP; while playing, a 24-PPQN clock
  at each tick's frame.
- **`rp.sms.sync`** clocks smsggdj: while playing, a 2-bit counter advanced each 24-PPQN tick, each step a
  level word at the tick's frame that the system holds on the sync lines (controller port 2's TR + TH on a
  Master System, the EXT port on a Game Gear, by `machine`).
- **`rp.lsdj.sync`** runs its `mode`, reading its routed MIDI and then the controller's launches as one
  inbox, in that order: MidiSync (a 24-PPQN `0xF8` clock at each tick's frame, `tempoDivisor`-subdivided,
  `autoStart` tapping START on the transport's rise), MidiSyncArduinoboy (notes 24/25 play and stop,
  26-29 set the divisor, 30 and up a row byte, `0xFA`/`0xFC` on transport edges, its clocks at frame 0),
  MidiMap (a NoteOn a row byte, the matching NoteOff `0xFE`, `0xFF` clocks at frame 0), KeyboardMidi (PS/2
  scancodes, sliding the octave cursor), MidiPassthrough (every byte verbatim), MidiOut (ArduinoboyMaster:
  last block's serial-out bytes decoded to host MIDI), and MasterSync (LSDj clocks itself: a `0xF8` a byte,
  the first of a run after the song-row NoteOn and `0xFA`, and `0xFC` once 200 ms pass with no byte, timed
  on the bytes' frames); Off and Keyboard send nothing. Its serial-in bytes go as runs of same-frame bytes,
  a run a message; a button press as `[button, down]` on `buttons` at frame 0; its host MIDI at frame 0. Its
  scratch is one bag kept across mode changes, master sync's sub-object dropped outside that mode so coming
  back starts clean. `serialOut` is a feedback wire from its Game Boy: last block's captured bytes, each at
  the frame its core completed it.
- **`rp.controller.session`** runs a `ControllerSession` ([controller/session.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/controller/session.ts))
  for the app its settings name (`controller/apps/index.ts`, the apps' runtime, zod-free): the surface's
  traffic and the block's clock in (its tick derived from ppq at 24 PPQN), its LED bytes out on
  `controllerOut`, and its row launches at frame 0 on `launches` (into the target cart's `rp.lsdj.sync`) or
  `midiOut` (out of the host, to a real Game Boy's Arduinoboy). It takes a device on the block a link first
  reports one. Its settings are what the control plane resolved: it parses nothing. A settings change that
  keeps the app, target, system and app config adopts a new timing table in place, so the playhead does not
  move; any other rebuilds the session around the same predictor, so the song does not restart; an anchor
  is applied once per `anchorSeq`.

**The drift-exact PPQ clock, in JS.** Native owns no `nextTick`/`eachTick` primitive.
[`walkTicks`](../packages/retroplug/src/ticks.ts#L23) is a faithful TS twin of native `PpqUtil::eachTick`:
it walks the ticks at `resolution` ticks a quarter that fall in this block, calling `cb(tick,
offsetSamples)` for each. A node that clocks keeps its `nextTick` on its instance
([nodes/clock.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/clock.ts) `TickClock`), and no system has two
clocking protocols, so it is the counter its system has; across blocks each tick fires exactly once, never
doubled or missed, and a jump of more than a tick (a seek, a loop, a start) resyncs. The transport it reads
is the block's, at the block-start ppq.

**Capacities.** Each output declares its queue
([nodes/ports.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes/ports.ts)): `serialIn` and `midi` 4096 messages /
72 KiB, what `rp.host.midi-in`'s output holds with 8 KiB more for a role's own bytes, so a SysEx the host
stages whole reaches the system whole and host MIDI is dropped only at that edge; a routing output what
`rp.host.midi-in`'s holds (2048 / 64 KiB), since under send-to-all it carries everything; `bytes` 256 / 1
KiB, `buttons` 64 / 128 bytes, `midiOut` 1024 / 8 KiB, `controllerOut` 256 / 4 KiB, `launches` 64 / 256
bytes. A send past one is dropped and counted (`Engine::droppedMessages`).

**Frame order.** A queue is frame-ordered: a message pushed with an earlier frame than the one before it is
raised to that frame. `rp.lsdj.sync` sends out of order onto `serialIn` in two modes: Arduinoboy MIDI sync
writes a row byte at its note's frame, then START / STOP and its clocks at frame 0, and MI.MAP writes row
bytes at their note's frame, then its `0xFF` clocks at frame 0. Both drive only a Game Boy, whose serial
queue begins a byte only once every byte ahead of it has gone, so raising a byte's frame to the one before
it changes nothing the core sees.

**A throw** in a node's JS is caught by the script host and counted (`Engine::scriptThrows`; the first one
is logged): what the node sent before it stands, a held serial-in run included, and the next block runs
again; the other nodes run as usual. A call that runs past the script host's CPU-time deadline is stopped
the same way, except that it skips the `finally` that sends the run, so that is cleared at the next
`process` instead; a second expiry in a row faults the node, and a fault outlives reshapes (only a rebuild,
or the node removed and added again, clears it).

**Settings without zod.** A node's settings are a zod-free schema
([graph/settingsSchema.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema.ts): `s.object`, `s.enum`,
`s.int`, `s.bool`, `s.number`, `s.string`, `s.array`, `s.json`), each builder parsing and writing its JSON
Schema as its zod twin did, so the bundle every Engine loads into both of its script runtimes holds no zod
(78 KB, where the kernel's was 660 KB, most of it zod). `defineNode` takes any schema with `safeParse` and
`toJSONSchema`, so a zod schema still serves on the control plane. The role's own zod schema stays on the
control plane: the store parses a role's config with it, and that parsed config is the node's settings.
[bundle-no-zod.test.ts](../packages/retroplug/test/script/bundle-no-zod.test.ts) fails the build of any
bundle that pulls a zod module, or a role or config module, back in.

## Store → graph

[`buildGraph`](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph.ts) places, in document order and ahead of the
systems (the planner breaks ties by document order, so they run first, and a profile build's `apu-render`
span relies on it):

1. `routing`, the `rp.midi.route` node, when the model has a MIDI routing mode (a project always has one;
   a `DirectGraph`, or a `SystemsStore` used without a project, routes none until a mode is set), fed from
   `midi-in.midi`;
2. `controller`, the `rp.controller.session` node, when a controller is enabled, fed from
   `controller-in.midi` and `.connected`, its `controllerOut` to `controller-out`;
3. each system's protocol nodes, in slot order and then the order of its roles, each `sys-<id>/<kind>`
   with the role's parsed config as its settings: what reads MIDI is fed from `routing.sys-<id>`, each
   output wired to the system node's input of the same name, a Game Boy's `serialOut` back into its
   `rp.lsdj.sync` as a feedback wire (one block late: what MI.OUT and master sync decode), and the
   controller's `launches` into the target system's `rp.lsdj.sync` when the target is `"system"`.

Which role kind is placed as which node, and how each type is wired, is one pure, zod-free table,
[graph/protocolNodes.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/protocolNodes.ts) (`protocolNodeOf`,
`protocolPipeline`): both stores and a `DirectGraph` read it, with or without a role registry, and a role
with no node is left out, so an edit to it (a model, a palette, an asset override) leaves the document as
it was. `test/system-settings/registry.test.ts` holds it to what `registerDspRoles` registers.

The rest of the document follows from those nodes:

- **Host MIDI out**: `rp.host.midi-out` in its systems form, its inputs in the order the kernel emitted:
  the controller's `midiOut` first (under its resolved target), then each `rp.lsdj.sync`'s in slot order,
  each under its system; with no producer, an empty list and no inputs.
- **The N8 cart mirror** (`cart`, `rp.n8.cart-mirror`) for the first NES in slot order, fed what that
  system's protocol nodes send its `midi` and `bytes` inputs.
- **The controller** ([graph/controller.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/controller.ts)): its target
  "0 is the first system" is resolved here (`controllerTarget`), so it follows a change of first system;
  with no system its host MIDI is tagged `NO_SYSTEM` (4294967295) and the node takes 0, its none. The
  publisher hands it the app config already parsed by the app's own schema (`parseAppConfig`,
  [controller/registry.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/controller/registry.ts)) and the timing table it read
  from the cart's battery, on the control plane. The `rp.lsdj.sync` node of the cart the MI.MAP app drives
  is forced to `midiMap`, or to `off` when the cart's own SYNC setting is not MI.MAP
  (`controllerSyncOverride`): that node's settings alone, so nothing reaches the `.rplg`.

Where nothing produces for a system input, or no controller is enabled, the input or the host I/O node is
left unwired. The plugin loads nothing for any of this
([pluginControlPlane.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/pluginControlPlane.ts)): the graph the project
publishes carries every node and its settings.

## Not yet built / deferred

Only the pieces below are open; the [07-remaining-work.md](07-remaining-work.md) doc is the authoritative
inventory of remaining work.

- **Raw Keyboard mode is the one unbuilt LSDj sync mode.** `rp.lsdj.sync` runs every other mode:
  MidiSync, MidiSyncArduinoboy, MidiMap, KeyboardMidi, MidiPassthrough, and the two host-out directions
  **MidiOut** (ArduinoboyMaster MI.OUT, serial out decoded to host MIDI) and **MasterSync**, with a
  live-apply menu. Raw **Keyboard** (mode 4) still sends nothing: it needs a per-block `keys` feed, an
  input on the node that nothing in the running host would feed yet, and per-block host `buttons` the same.
- **The MI.OUT and master-sync decoders allocate.** Their emitted arrays cost about 3 JS allocations for
  every host MIDI message they decode, the one per-block JS allocation left on a production path; it is
  the decoders' own change, in `lsdjArduinoboy.ts`.
- **kit-patch UI-thread behaviour.** LSDj kit-patch runs entirely on the UI / control thread: it
  compiles the kit (over the native `KitCompiler` primitives) and the `lsdj-assets` role folds it into the
  ROM in memory. It has **no protocol node** and never reaches the audio thread. A role-owned settings UI
  would need the deferred `ui?` render seam.
- **`ui?` render descriptor + extension model.** The `ui?` field on `RoleType` is a labelled-deferred
  seam (a role's own settings UI), and the third-party extension model (registering `RoleType`s, ROM
  providers, and node types from outside the built-ins) is future work.

## Key files

TypeScript ([packages/retroplug/src/](../packages/retroplug/src/)):

- [systemRoles.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/systemRoles.ts): `RoleInstance` / `RoleType` /
  `RoleRegistry` / `RomProvider` / `ConstructCaps`.

- [script/nodes/](../packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes): the seven node types, `clock.ts` (the tick
  counter) and `ports.ts` (the capacities); [ticks.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/ticks.ts): `walkTicks`.

  [graph/controller.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/controller.ts) /
  [graph/buildGraph.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph.ts): store → graph, the protocol node per
  role, the controller's target and its cart's sync override.
- [graph/settingsSchema.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema.ts) /
  [graph/defineNode.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/graph/defineNode.ts): the zod-free settings schema and the
  node contract.

  [script/register.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/script/register.ts): the bundle every Engine embeds, and how
  a bundle registers its node types.
- [controller/apps/index.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/controller/apps/index.ts) /
  [controller/registry.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/controller/registry.ts): the controller apps' runtime,
  and their labels and schemas for the control plane.
- [appHost.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/appHost.ts): `buildAppRegistry`.

Native ([packages/native/src/](../packages/native/src/)):

- [ScriptHost.hpp](../packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.hpp) /
  [ScriptHost.cpp](../packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.cpp): the script-node runtime the
  protocol nodes run in.
- [SystemNodes.cpp](../packages/native/src/host/graph/SystemNodes.cpp): each system node's inputs,
  applied before its core runs.
- [HostIoNodes.cpp](../packages/native/src/host/graph/HostIoNodes.cpp): the host I/O nodes the protocol
  nodes read from and send to, and the N8 cart mirror.
- [EngineRpcService.cpp](../packages/native/src/host/rpc/EngineRpcService.cpp#L165): `applyRoleConfig`
  (system-role only).

-

 refilled in place, its payloads copied into one JS-owned buffer:
 [ScriptHost.cpp](../packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.cpp) `fillMessages`), so a node written
 with indexed loops allocates nothing per block once warm: a message's `data` view is made again only when
 its place in the payload buffer moves, and the pool and the buffer grow only past their largest block.

-(`kernelNode.ts` `blockInput`, deleted in B3b): an `input` object and its

-freed after the call, so this is per-block garbage, and it grows with the block's message count.

The emulated queue is unbounded and instant by default, so a ROM can never be starved and never loses a byte; `setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware" })` + `reset(id)` gives it the cartridge's 2048-byte depth and ~150 KB/s wire (spec/04).
